The Fairlady name* was used for the first time with the SPL213 (1,200cc, 60PS) launched in 1961. This model can be traced back to the Datsun Sports (S211), which was launched in June 1959. The SPL212 (1,200cc, 43PS) and SPL213 (1,200cc, 55PS) engines - improved versions of the S211 (1,000cc, 34PS) - were originally used exclusively for export models. The name "Fairlady" appeared on the domestic market with the launch of the Fairlady 1500 (SP310) in October 1962. In May 1963, an S310 powered by the Cedric's 71PS engine easily beat an array of foreign sports cars in the 1st Japan GP (B-II race), thereby demonstrating to the whole world the high standard attained by Japan's sports cars. The Fairlady 1600 (SP311) was launched in May 1965 as an upgraded model. It was equipped with the 1,595cc, 90PS R engine, first used in the first-generation Silvia, and a Porsche-type 4-speed full-synchromesh transmission. In March 1967, at the time the Fairlady 2000 (SR311) was launched, there was a minor change to the SP311 that chiefly concerned the interior. In November of the same year, another minor change was carried out to ensure the car conformed to US safety standards. This commemorative car is the North American export model with left-hand drive. It differs slightly in specifications and exterior design from the domestic model, one example being the bumper overriders. *During a trip to the US, Katsuji Kawamata, former President of Nissan, was so moved by the long-running musical "My Fair Lady" that he decided to name the upcoming SPL213 after it. It was his wish that the new car, like the musical, would prove to be popular over many years.

The engine size of the second generation DATSUN Fairlady started with 1500cc on "1500" in 1962. It finally reached 2000cc on "Fairlady 2000" SR311 in 1967. The combination of U20 engine (1,982cc, 4-cyl. inline, OHC) and SOLEX twin carburetor generated the max. output of 145ps and achieved the max. speed of 205km/h via 5-speed MT with Porsche type synchromesh. SR311 was known as the first Japanese car that broke through a wall of 200km/h. It also achieved good results in races such as Japan GP 1967 and Rallye Monte-Carlo in 1968. It was often seen at events until the release of the successor Fairlady Z in 1969. This is a left-hand-drive car for export to US.

The first generation Datsun Sunny, rolled out in April 1966, was developed mainly by younger engineers including ZenzoSonoda, the supervisor. The 1-liter “A” OHV engine generated 56ps. Its clean and sporty styling, the high performance of 20.6 second for the standing start quarter mile and the maximum speed of 135km/h appealed many users. The 4-door sedan type was rolled out in April 1967 and the sports series with 4-speed manual floorshiftand the 3-speed automatic transmission type were added. The Sunny had a wide variation of types such as trucks and coupes and became one of the most popular models of Nissan. This car is a “Sports Deluxe” grade.

The first generation Datsun Sunny 1000 that opened the door to "the era of private cars" in Japan was released in April 1966 as a Datsun brand car. The original lineup was 2-door sedan and van. Sunny 1000 4-door van and Sunny truck (B20) were added in 1967. Linear exterior was shared with van and sedan, but here is a trivia; when developing the model, van was designed first, and sedan was designed based on van. Sunny 1000 van was a stylish commercial vehicle with an air of sedan and met a multitude of needs. This car is "Datsun Sunny 1000 Van Deluxe" after a minor change in 1968.

The first generation Laurel (C30) was developed as a small-size luxury car line positioned between Bluebird and Cedric and released in 1968. It started up the time when sedans were classified not by engines or body sizes but by their concepts or drivers' lifestyles. Mounted engine was newly developed G18 (4-cyl. inline, OHC, 1800cc) that was to be mounted on Skyline. It was equipped with 4-wheel independent suspension of strut unit for front wheels and semi-trailing arm type for rear wheels, like the third generation Bluebird (510), to realize better road holding performance. Nissan's first pillarless 2-door hardtop and G20 engine (2000cc, OHC) were added in 1970.

Nissan R381 is a Group 7 racing car especially built for 1968 Japan Grand Prix (GP race). The biggest characteristic of the machine is the active split rear wings named “Aero Stabilizer” whose left wing and right wing coordinate with the rear suspension, move independently while running, and move together at braking. The R381 machines with this characteristic wings were called “Griffin.” This car is No.20, driven by Moto Kitano that won the championship of the 1968 GP race.

A new high-end passenger car "President" (150) was rolled out in 1965 as a successor of Cedric Special (50). The concept of exterior was the harmony of curved lines with aerodynamic performance. Two types of engine were adopted; 6-cyl. in line and 2,974cc for limousines, and V8 3,988cc and 180ps with oil tappet and silent chain for quietness. Comfortability was realized by items such as the first power steering system on domestic vehicles, heated rear window, dimming rear-view mirror, variable speed wiper, remote-control side mirrors and air conditioner for rear seat to be one of the best cars in Japan. This is "C-spec" car in 1968 with V8 engine.

The third generation Skyline C10 was released in 1968. The nickname "Hakosuka (Boxy Skyline)" came from its boxy styling. The first generation "2000GT-R", the symbol of the third generation Skyline, made a debut in 1969. The lineup of C10 Skyline included commercial vehicles "Estate" and "Van". They were popular as stylish commercial vehicles because they also had "Surfin' Line" coming from the Sedan series. Mounted engine was "G15" (4-cyl.in line SOHC, 1500cc, 88ps) that was developed for the last model of the second generation. G18 engine (1800cc, 100ps) was added in 1969. The rear suspension of the 1500 series including commercial vehicles was rigid axle type with parallel leaf springs.

The second-generation Cedric, the H130, was launched in October 1965. It was designed by the Italian carrozzeria Pininfarina. The H130 was also the first to feature a 6-cylinder in line OHC engine (L20) that was to be used for the next two decades. Since its launch, minor changes were carried out every autumn, and by September 1968 the interior of the car as well as its styling had changed considerably.

The second generation Cedric 130 was released after a full-model change in 1965 when Japan is amid the high economic growth period. The refined styling by Italian carrozzeria Pininfarina followed the European design trend at the time. It was an epoch-making model because mounted was the first L20 engine (6-cyl. In line, OHC) that was the core engine of Nissan for the following 20 years. A minor change was made almost every autumn, and in 1968, the form was changed to flat and square styling with no remnant of the original model. Special 6Ewas the highest-grade model. This car is the model after a minor change in 1969. L20 engine (single carburetor, 115ps) is mounted.

Launched in October 1965, the distinguishing feature of the second-generation model (130) was its prestigious style, designed by the Italian carrozzeria, Pininfarina. The Special 6 anticipated the era of high-speed transport by using a 6-cylinder in line OHC engine (L20); it also had disc brakes fitted as standard. In September 1968, the front end and rear end were significantly redesigned, after which it was referred to as the "late model".

The third generation Bluebird 510 was rolled out in August 1967 and immediately acquired a very good reputation because of a sharp body shape with no ventilation windows, high basic performance and usefulness realized by advanced mechanisms such as the OHC engine and four-wheel independent suspension. The global sales reached more than a million and a half in 5 years. Many people still call it "Five-Ten," an endearing nickname. This model was highly esteemed in the motor sport scene for the overall victory at the 18th East-African Safari Rally in 1970. Some people even said that this model had rewritten performance criteria of this class. This car is "1600 Deluxe" equipped with single carburetor L16 engine of 92ps.

The third generation Datsun Bluebird 510 was rolled out in August 1967. It started with sedans of 2 doors / 4 doors and station wagons / vans of 5 doors. The engine variation was 1.3-liter L13 of inline 4-cylinder OHC, and 1.6-liter L16 to be mounted on 1600SSS (Super Sport Sedan). It became very popular for the sharp body lines, excellent basic performance and usability. The global sales reached more than 1.55 million in 5 years. The 2-door coupe series was added in November 1968 in Japanese market. The sedan "1600SSS" won in both the overall and the team categories at the 18th East-African Safari Rally in 1970. This car is Coupe 1600SSS with L16 twin-carburetor 100ps engine.

The first generation DATSUN Sunny 1000 that opened the door to "The Age of private cars" in Japan was rolled out in April 1966. It was a DATSUN car with variations of 2-door sedan and van. 4-door and truck (B20) were added in 1967 and smartish fastback coupe was added in 1968 to increase the number of variations. Coupe was greatly favored by mostly young people as a stylish and affordable private car. 4-cyl. OHV engine of 1000cc generated 60ps. The floor shift transmission and the car weight as light as 675kg helped to create the image that Sunny is a sporty compact car. This car is manufactured in 1969 and colored in "Sun-kissed Yellow" that match up with Sunny's image of "Sun".

After a big campaign to advertise for names, Nissan released Datsun Sunny 1000 B10, the all-new affordable passenger car, in April 1966. It became a big hit among younger people because of its youthful image, brisk ride and low prices of 410,000 yen for standard and 460,000 yen for deluxe. The original lineup of Sunny 1000 included commercial van. Another commercial vehicle of pickup truck "Sunny Truck" was added in 1967. The low price of 365,000 yen, high output of 56ps, modern styling and the minimum turning radius of 4m overwhelmed competing trucks and Sunny truck became very popular. This is the model after the minor change in October 1968.

The first generation "FairladyZ" S30, also known as Datsun 240Z or "Z-car", was rolled out in December 1969 and won a big market not only in Japan but in North America and other countries. This model was manufactured for nine years as a representative car of Nissan all over the world and its global sales was over 520,000 units, the best number on record for sport cars of a single model. This car is the high performance Model "Z432" on which "S20" engine of an inline 6-cylinder 4-valve DOHC and 160ps is mounted. This engine is same as that of the third generation Skyline 2000GT-R (PGC10). "432" comes from the engine configuration of S20, i.e. "4 valves, 3 carburetors, and 2 camshafts." The standard equipment included LSD (limited slip differential) and luxurious magnesium wheels appropriate for the flagship model. The sticker price was 1.85 million yen that was almost double of the basic Z-car.

The third generation "Nissan Gloria A30" made a debut in April 1967 after Prince Motors, Ltd. merged with Nissan Motor Co., Ltd. The development was substantially made by former Prince, but some of the parts and components were shared with Nissan cars. For example, the unique De Dion rear suspension of the Gloria was changed to the conventional parallel leaf rigid. The A30's styling looked like a limousine "Nissan Prince Royal" that was unveiled in 1966, and its long and wide body was called "Royal line." Its 2-liter OHC "G7" engine of Prince Motors since 1963 was changed to "L20" engine of Nissan in October 1969. This car is 1969 Nissan Gloria "Super Deluxe" with the G7 engine. After the fourth generation model "Gloria 230" rolled out in 1971, Gloria shared the body with the Nissan Cedric.

"Grand Prix race" was the race of the highest rank in Japan Grand Prix about which many Japanese were enthusiastic in the late 1960s. Nissan R382 is a "Group 7" provisions-compliant prototype race car that was developed for the GP in 1969. Mounted engine was GRX-III, newly developed 6-liter V12 DOHC, generated more than 600ps. M. Kurosawa/Y. Sunako drove No.21 and won first place and M. Kitano/T. Yokoyama drove No.20 and won second place, marking the 2nd straight victory of Nissan. Japan GP was discontinued in 1970 with increasing social issues around automobiles. This car is the 10th place car No.23 which was driven by K. Takahashi/K. Tohira in the race.

Grand Prix race" was the race of the highest rank in Japan Grand Prix about which many Japanese were enthusiastic in the late 1960s. Nissan R382 is a "Group 7" provisions-compliant prototype race car that was developed for the GP in 1969. Mounted engine was GRX-III, newly developed 6-liter V12 DOHC, generated more than 600ps. MotoharuKurosawa drove No.21 and won first place and Moto Kitano drove No.20 and won second place, marking the 2nd straight victory of Nissan. Japan GP was discontinued in 1970 with increasing social issues around automobiles. This car is the genuine overall winner No.21.

"Skyline 2000 GT-R (PGC10)", a high performance sedan for touring car races with world's first 4-valve DOHC engine fro production cars, was released as a variation of the third generation Skyline C10 in 1969. This is the origin of "GT-R". Its first race was "JAF GP" in Fuji Int'l Speedway in May 1969. Most participants were clubman drivers. Many GT-R machines of Prince Motorist Club·Sports (PMC·S)* participated but most of them retired due to the difficulty of driving a high-spec machine. As a result, T. Shinohara on No.39 won on points. It was a narrow win for GT-R that would win many races in the future. This is the overall winner No.39 spec car of JAF GP in 1969, driven by T. Shinohara. *PMC·S. Prince Motorist Club-Sports, that has participated in motor sports since 1964, with Skyline and NISSAN GT-R.

Nissan combined its best technologies and produced “Skyline 2000GT-R” in February 1969 after merging with Prince Motors, Ltd. “GT-R” was a high performance car produced for touring car races. The know-how for prototype race car "R380" was filled in an ordinary looking sedan body*. Mounted was the 4-valve DOHC engine re-engineered from the one for R380 to suit production cars. It made a debut and won at “JAF GP” in May 1969, 3 months after the rollout. Since then, it kept winning until it attained 52 victories before the Nissan works team withdrew in October 1972. *The body changed to 2-door hardtop in the autumn of 1970.

The first generation Cherry made a debut in 1970 as the Nissan's first front-wheel drive (FWD) car and gained a high recognition especially in Europe. Rear-wheel drive (RWD) was being replaced with FWD in small-sized cars in those days because FWD layout could realize both compact body and large interior space. Most of compact cars today adopt it for this reason. The name "Cherry" came from the cherry tree for Japaneseness. Gently-curved body named capsule shape and J-shaped side window lines were the exterior features. Coupe of a bold design was added in 1971. This car is 2-door sedan with standard A10 engine of 58ps.

The first generation Cherry made a debut in 1970 as the Nissan's first FF (front engine, front-wheel drive) car and gained a high recognition especially in Europe. FR (front engine, rear-wheel drive) was being replaced with FF in small-sized cars in those days because FF layout could realize both compact body and large interior space. Most of compact cars today adopt it for this reason. The name "Cherry" came from the cherry tree for Japaneseness. Gently-curved body named capsule shape and J-shaped side window lines were the exterior features. Coupe of a bold design was added in 1971. This car is 4-door sedan "X-1" with A12 engine of 80ps and SU type twin carburetors.

In August of 1967, the Datsun Bluebird was fully remodelled to the third generation "510". The 510, as well as the past DATSUN cars, gradually proved its high potential through grueling international rallies. And finally the 1600SSS won the 18th East-African Safari Rally in all the categories of Overall/Class/Team in 1970. This is the historic first win as a domestic car and an accomplishment of Nissan since its first challenge to this rally in 1963. This model is well-known as "a great car on screen" because it was this model that Yujiro Ishihara, one of the best actors in the Showa era, drove as his own machine in the movie "Safari 5000" released in July, 1969.

Datsun Sunny 1200 B110 was released in 1970 after the first generation 1000. With the image of a family car, it evolved into a car with abundant appealing items. The copy "A car next door looks smaller" is still talked about. Mounted A12 engine (4-cyl.in line OHV, 1171cc) was utilized so much that it was admired as one of the best-performing engines in motor sports. Interior space was largest in the class and interiors such as meters and seats were of rich-conscious designs. Mechanisms of upper grade including auto-ventilation system and shock-absorbing instrument panel were adopted. This is Sunny "1200GL" grade that was used in advertising when the model was released.

This is the second generation Datsun Sunny (B110 series), rolled out as a family car in January 1970. The advertising tagline in Japan was "Car next door looks small." The model started with a wide variation of 14 sedan types with 2 doors / 4 doors, 4 coupe types of 2 doors, and 4 types of van. The 4-door sedan had the maximum room space in the class and was especially popular among many people as the hallmark of Sunny. The A12 engine of 4-cylinder OHV 1171cc generated 68ps. It secured the handling and stability, the comfortable riding as good as that of higher class cars, and the maximum speed of 150km/h.

The first generation DATSUN Sunny 1000 B10 made a debut in 1966. Sunny sedan was an epoch-making car that triggered the age of private cars in Japan. Sunny 1000 van VB10 was rolled out simultaneously as a handy passenger and cargo vehicle and became very popular. The next generation was DATSUN Sunny 1200 Van VB110 on which A12 engine (1200cc, 4-cyl. inline, OHV, 68ps) was mounted like sedan and coupe. Usability was greatly improved by the 4-door design and the tailgate with balancer. This car is "Deluxe" in 1970. The production of the brother car Sunny Truck was continued after discontinuation of sedan, coupe and van until 1994 in Japan and 2008 in overseas markets.

In 1969, "Datsun Fairlady" (also known as Datsun Sports / Roadster) was transformed from a convertible to a GT car "Fairlady Z (also known as Datsun Z)" S30 on which a driver could ride comfortably and enjoy cruising. Its lower, longer and wider styling created an aura of elegance and fierceness, which captured many people. Performance was of the first grade. "240Z" with the engine of 2400cc and 150ps demonstrated its potential by achieving good results in motor sports. The first generation "Z", also called "Z-Car", was famous as a biggest-selling sports car in the world with the worldwide sales for 8 years up to 1978 of 520,000. Z was admired passionately by many people. This car is "Z-L", the upper grade model in the earliest days.

TGloria was born as a high-end passenger car of Prince Motors and later became a variant model of Nissan Cedric. The third generation Gloria A30 was released in 1967 and attracted attention as "Nissan Gloria". It was the first new model after Nissan and Prince merged but was virtually a car developed by former Prince. One of the features was the front mask with vertically aligned 4-bulb type headlamps that resembled "Nissan Prince Royal", a VIP limousine developed by Prince. And the well-proportioned and wide styling gained popularity. This is the last model manufactured in 1970. G7 engine designed by Prince was replaced with L20 engine (6-cyl. in line, SOHC, 2000cc) designed by Nissan.

The first generation Laurel C30 rolled out in 1968 was an innovative vehicle, different from Bluebird 510 and Cedric 130, that created a new category of "the car for high-class owners". One of the features was advanced technologies such as G18 engine (1800cc, 4-cyl. inline, OHC of cross-flow type), 4-wheel independent suspension of strut/semi trailing arm, and rack-and-pinion steering. Its stately and elegant form was also a selling point. A model with G20 engine (2000cc) and a model of Nissan's first pillar-less 2-door hardtop were added in 1970. This car is 2000GX of the highest grade in hardtop series with vinyl chloride leather roof that was in fashion at the time.

The development of the new machine "R383" was launched for a three-peat of Japan Grand Prix after R381's victory in 1968 and R382's in 1969. The engine would be the same with that of R382 (GRX-III; V12, DOHC, 5954cc) with the output exceeding 700ps. It would be 900ps in the turbocharged specs for races of CAN-AM series. But Japan GP was discontinued in 1970 due to changes in circumstances around automobiles and the battlefield for R383 was lost. That's why it was called "phantom machine." This car was restored to the drivable condition like other R38 series cars and demonstrated its first run at NISMO FESTIVAL in 2006 after 36 years since it was developed.

The third generation Skyline C10 was born in 1968 after a full-model change. It was famous for its nickname "Hakosuka (Boxy Skyline)". Features included wider and lower body and edgy styling. Especially the character line on the rear fender was designed based on the hydrodynamics and later called "Surfin' Line". In August 1969, the 1800 series was added when a minor change was made and the legendary advertising campaign with the copy "Ai-no-Skyline (Skyline Of Love)" was started. Since then, Skyline became more and more recognized as grand touring car with its own identity. This car is 2000GT after the minor change with owner's modifications such as twin carburetors.

The FairladyZ, also known as the export model name "Datsun 240Z", challenged world rallies to prove its high performance. This car is the overall winner of the 19th East-African Safari Rally in 1971, and brought Nissan's second win in a row, following the victory in the previous year by the Datsun Bluebird. The engine mounted on the competition machine was L24 with in line 6-cylinder OHC 2393cc and generated 210ps. This car was restored by "Nissan Restoration Club" in 2013 to the drivable condition while preserving the appearance at the rally's finish line.

The third generation Skyline C10 was born in 1968 after a full-model change. It was famous for its nickname "Hakosuka (Boxy Skyline)". Features included wider and lower body and edgy styling. Especially the character line on the rear fender was designed based on the hydrodynamics and later called "Surfin' Line". The advertising campaign with the copy "Ai-no-Skyline (Skyline Of Love)" became legendary. The original lineup of 1500 series was "Standard" and "Deluxe", but "Family Deluxe", "Touring Deluxe" and "Sporty Deluxe" were added. Mounted engine was "G15" (4-cyl. OHC, 1500cc, 88ps) developed for the last model of the previous generation. This car is Sporty Deluxe manufactured in 1971.

The third generation Skyline C10 was born in 1968 after a full-model change. It was famous for its nickname "Hakosuka (Boxy Skyline)". Features included wider and lower body and edgy styling. Especially the character line on the rear fender was designed based on the hydrodynamics and later called "Surfin' Line". The advertising campaign with the copy "Ai-no-Skyline (Skyline Of Love)" became legendary. The original lineup of 1500 series was "Standard" and "Deluxe", but "Family Deluxe", "Touring Deluxe" and "Sporty Deluxe" were added. Mounted engine was "G15" (4-cyl. OHC, 1500cc, 88ps) developed for the last model of the previous generation. This car is Sporty Deluxe manufactured in 1971.

The third generation Cedric 230 released in 1971 was the first generation that shared basic structure with Gloria after Nissan merged with Prince Motors in 1966. Its elegant and graceful styling of moderately adopted coke bottle line gained very favorable reviews. Japan's first pillarless 4-door hardtop that had both beautiful styling and comfortability was added in 1972, which created a trend of domestic high-end cars for the following several decades. 230 sedan was often seen in police dramas televised years ago in Japan. This car is Cedric 2000GL Sedan with L20 engine. The leather-top roof is non-original feature.

The Fairlady 240Z, also known as the export model name "Datsun 240Z", participated in famous "Rallye Monte-Carlo" mainly on snowy and icy roads. In the 41st Rallye Monte-Carlo, the 240Z finished third, which surprised rally concerned people all over the world. The reason is that 240Z adopted the FR (front engine / rear wheel drive) system with the engine mounted in front. The FR system was thought to be disadvantageous on snow and ice, but the result betrayed the prediction. As a result, more and more drivers began driving Z-car at domestic rallies. This car is the one that finished third at the 41st Rallye Monte-Carlo in 1972 by Rauno Aaltonen and Jean Todt.

The second generation Datsun Sunny (B110) achieved good results in motor sports with the engine enhanced from 1000cc to 1200cc. 1200GX-5, 2-door coupe, added in August 1972 was heavily used as a base car for races. "5" of GX-5 stands for 5-speed floor-shift MT in which the reduction gear ratio is 1.000 at fifth. With A12 engine tuned up to 130ps and wide tires, it ran races in "TS Race" category of Fuji International Speedway and won championships from 1971 through 1974, in 1977, 1979, 1980 and 1982. This is the genuine car that was exhibited at Tokyo Motor Show in 1972. It was restored by Nissan Restoration Club in 2018.

The 520 was launched in May 1965. It became the 521 in February 1970 and, to meet the demands of the era of fast travel, the 1500 series was introduced. The 1300 too was subject to a minor change, adding a new radiator grille with horizontal emphasis and egg-shaped fender mirrors. There were 3 models available in the commercial-use Datsun series: the standard truck, van, and pickup.

"Datsun 240Z," equipped with 2.4-liter engine, was originally an exported model mainly to North America as of 1970. It went on sale also in Japan in November 1971 to respond to the request from customers. Three variations were available -Nissan Fairlady 240Z, 240Z-L, and 240ZG. The 240ZG's biggest exterior characteristic was the front end: so-called "G-nose" with the nose piece made of FRP, headlamp covers, and over fenders. The coefficient of drag (Cd) was the top-class performance of 0.390 among many other sport cars at that time, and the maximum speed reached 210km/h.

The first generation FairladyZ S30 (also known as Datsun 240Z) was developed as successor of Datsun Sports 2000 SR311 and released in December 1969 in Japan. It became a big hit not only in Japan but in foreign countries such as North America because of the beautiful styling, improved driving comfort and safety, high performance engine, 4-wheel independent suspension, and the affordable price. The initial lineup in Japan had only 2.0-liter engines, however, 2.4-liter engine series, as well as the exported editions, was added in 1971. This car is the fastest grade "240ZG" that was used as a police car of Kanagawa Prefectural Police since 1972, mainly on expressways. The travel distance of this car reached 370,940km in total.

The second generation Nissan Laurel C130 rolled out in 1972 was a luxurious car like the first generation C30 and also "a car with luxury and high quality that the owner can boast" in the 1970s. The copy "Drive easy, live easy" was sensational and went ahead of the times since Japan was still amid the high-growth period. The form of 4-door sedan and 2-door hardtop featured "Thunder streak", i.e., the side of body was pressed into "Z" shape. Especially 2-door was very popular because its form viewed from the rear looked like an American car. This car is "2000GL-6" in the early days with L20 single cab 115ps engine. Engine variations on C130 totaled 6 from 1800cc to 2800cc.

The second generation Patrol 60 remained a long-selling product from 1960 to 1980 when the next generation Safari 160 was released. Robust design of ladder frame and leaf rigid suspension was passed down from the first generation 4W60. 2WD and 4WD could be switched by a lever. The lineup was short body (the wheelbase of 2200mm), long body (the wheelbase of 2500mm), soft top/hard top/van/station wagon. It is also adopted as fire engine because of its powerful engine and mobility. In overseas markets, the name Patrol has been passed down since the first generation that was born in 1951. This is the most long-lasting name except "Nissan/Datsun Pickup". This car is Soft Top of Short Body.

The "Skyline 2000GT-R" first appeared in 1969 out of the third generation Skyline C10 and reached milestone of 50 victories at domestic touring car races within 2 years and 10 months. On the other hand, a new model of Skyline, Model C110, was introduced in September 1972. This car was a "Skyline 2000GT-R Racing Concept" car and was exhibited at the 19th Tokyo Motor Show held in 1972 after the introduction of the new model. Its car number was 73 which suggested the participation in races of the coming 1973 season. But the Nissan works team stopped operating because of tasks such as the development of anti-pollution technology and improvement of fuel efficiency. This car was fully restored by "Nissan Restoration Club" in 2007, 35 years after the unveiling, and ran at the NISMO FESTIVAL in the same year with applause and cheering.

Skyline 2000GT-R (PGC10) was a 4-door sedan rolled out in 1969, and it became invincible at domestic touring car races. It remodeled to 2-door hardtop (KPGC10) in 1970. The wheelbase was shortened by 70mm and the weight was lightened by more than 20kg by downsizing the body. As well as the sedan version, 2-liter, 4-valve DOHC inline 6-cyl. "S20" engine was mounted into which all the technologies of engine of a prototype racing car "Nissan R380" were applied. Hardtop cars also had a fuel tank of 100L, full bucket seats without recliner mechanism, and spartaninterior without amenities. GT-R attained unprecedented 50 victories in March 1972 at domestic touring car races. It has a record of 52 victories when Nissan works team stopped its activities in October 1972.

Skyline was fully remodeled to the third generation C10 in August 1968. The C10 was the first Skyline after Nissan Motor merged with Prince Motors. The series started with 4-door sedan with 1.5-liter and 2.0-liter engines and station wagon / van with a 1.5-liter engine, but the variation gradually became wider after "2000GT-R" with very high performance and 1.8-liter engine cars appeared. A new series of stylish "2-door hardtop" body with a shorter wheelbase by 70mm was rolled out in 1970. The "2000GT-X" with the engine of SU twin carburetor and the power 130ps was added in September 1971 as an upper model of the 2000GT line. This car is 2-door Hardtop 2000GT-X manufactured in 1972.

The third generation Cedric 230 released in 1971 was the first generation that shared the basic structure with Gloria after Nissan merged with Prince Motors in 1966. Its elegant and graceful styling of moderately adopted "coke bottle line" gained very favorable reviews, and unit sales exceeded that of Toyopet Crown. The original lineup was 4-door sedan, 2-door hardtop, station wagon and van. Mounted engine was L20 of 2000cc. L26 engine of 2600cc was added in 1971. Japan's first pillarless 4-door hardtop was added in 1972. 4-door hardtop created the trend of high-end cars to come. This car is 4-door Hardtop Custom Deluxe with L20 engine and the sticker price was 1,150,000yen.

The Cherry debuted as Nissan's first FF car in October 1970, with the same A10 and A12 engines as those in the Sunny. In November of the following year, a coupe was added to the lineup. The top-tier "X-1" model was powered by the SU twin-carb A12 (80ps) engine and attracted many younger drivers. In the 1972 Fuji GC Series Minor Touring class, it performed well alongside the Sunny, which won that year's title.

The Fairlady Z (S30) was launched as the 2000 series in November 1969. Two years later in November 1971, the 240Z was added to the domestic lineup (it had previously only been available as a North American export model). Offering high power and superior maneuverability, the 240Z did well in overseas rallies, coming in 1st overall in the 1971 and 1973 Safari Rally. This commemorative car is the No.1 car that won in 1973, driven by S. Mehta and Lofty Drews.

At the 21st East Africa Safari Rally in 1973, the same Nissan team's Fairlady 240Z having just become the overall champion, this 1800SSS (H. Carlstrom ) performed brilliantly, coming in 2nd overall and winning its class, thus ensuring that people around the world would associate the name "Nissan" with car rallies. The 610's debut was in August 1971. There were two series, the 1.6-liter and 1.8-liter.

The second-generation Sunny, launched in January 1970, was significantly larger, with an overall length of 3,830mm (+30mm), an overall width of 1,495mm (+45mm), and a wheelbase of 2,300mm (+20mm). April of the following year saw the addition of the Excellent Series (Sedan/Coupe), high-grade models equipped with the L14 engine. H. Kitano's No. 2 car won the 1973 Japan GP (TS race).

In November 1971, "240Z" with 2,400cc engine included in the Fairlady Z lineup in Japan. The top-of-the-line model, the 240ZG, featured a 190mm long nose, headlight covers and over-fenders as standard. This car is the test car for the Omori factory, which had an L28 engine with crossflow combustion chambers.

This is the fourth generation Skyline that became very popular by the copy "Skyline for Ken and Mary." However, this "2000GT-R" model was manufactured for only 4 months from January to April of 1973 and the total number of manufactured cars was less than 200 due to the stricter emission standards. Along with the fact that it didn't participate in touring car races, this model is still called "Phantom GT-R." Intake air duct, disc brakes for four wheels, mesh front grille, over fenders on wheels, and the exterior with a rear spoiler as standard equipment also attracted attention. But it was very rare even in those days for people to see this model running.

However, this "2000GT-R" model was manufactured for only 4 months from January to April of 1973 and the total number of manufactured cars was less than 200 due to the stricter emission standards.
