Intake air duct, disc brakes for four wheels, mesh front grille, over fenders on wheels, and the exterior with a rear spoiler as standard equipment also attracted attention. But it was very rare even in those days for people to see this model running.

Launched in January 1973, the Violet was positioned between the Sunny and the Bluebird U. There were 1,400cc and 1,600cc engines, and both the sedan and hardtop had a long nose and fastback for a sporty silhouette. Furthermore, the hardtop's rear window was unusual in using recurved glass.

The fourth Skyline C110 generation, released in September, 1972, inherited the unique feature of the predecessor with expanded body size. Its distinct "Surfin' Line" was changed to soft and elegant style. The iconic four ring-shaped taillights, modeled after a jet engine nozzle, was first adopted in this model. Stemming from the previous advertisement campaign known as the "Skyline Love", the new "Ken & Mary's Skyline" campaign became a mega hit with its original T-shirts sales. It became a social phenomenon during the sales period of five years and the total sales of C110/C111 under the nick name of "Ken & Mary" had broken 0.66 million. This model was 2000GT, a 1974 model year car, and it was recoated in the initial image color: "Bright Blue Metallic".

The fourth generation Bluebird 610 released in 1971 was named "Bluebird U" from a strategic point of view to upgrade its image to a high-end car. Mounted engines were L (4-cyl. OHC, 1600cc and 1800cc) and there were variations of single carburetor, SU type twin carburetors and electronically controlled fuel infection system (EGI) for 1800cc. In 1973, 2000 GT series (G610) was added. Mounted engine was L20 (6-cyl.in line, 2000cc) that was the same as the one on Skyline. One of the features was the styling with long nose and the look gave it a nickname of "Shark Face". This car is 4-door sedan 2000 GTX and mounted L20 engine with SU type twin carburetors generates 125ps.

The first generation Cherry E10, Nissan's first front-wheel drive (FWD) car, underwent a full model change to Cherry F-II F10 in 1974 with enlarged body sizes and engine. Lineup was sedan, coupe, and van. Engine variations were 1200cc and 1400cc. It had soft and curvy form and details were uniquely designed with the motif of hexagon. Impact absorbing structure and 3-point type seatbelts were installed to answer the increased safety awareness. It got favorable reviews by the name of "DATSUN 120A" in overseas markets as well as E10. This car is 4-door sedan 1400GL in 1975 of the original specifications that was driven by a single owner for more than 40 years.

The fourth generation Bluebird U 610 was rolled out in 1971 as a successor of the famous DATSUN Bluebird 510. "U"stands for both USER and YOU. It has sweeping form and one of the features is J-shaped line of side windows. The engine of the predecessor was mainly 1600cc but 610 had 2 types of engines of 1600cc 4-cylinder OHC and 1800cc 4-cylinder OHC in early days. 2000GT (G610) with the engine of 2000cc 6-cylinder, the same type with that of Skyline, was added in 1973. This is Sedan 1600GL of the later days with L16 engine of 100ps. Disk brakes for front wheels, wooden steering, and rear window with heating coil are included as standard.

Datsun Sunny led the motorization of Japan since 1966 and the third generation Sunny B210 was rolled out in 1973. 1400cc engine model was added to the previous generation in 1971 and 1400cc model of B210 was also called "Sunny Excellent". Forms of sedan and coupe were changed to curvy ones. Especially the form of coupe was very unique with handy tailgate like "Fairlady Z" and "coda tronca" type of tail end. Horizontally aligned 6 round taillamps of Excellent Coupe were also talked about. Collapsible steering wheel, seat belts, head rests, and front disc brakes were widely adopted in terms of safety. This is Sunny Excellent 1400 GL with L14 engine of 1428cc, 85ps.

The fourth generation Gloria 230 released in 1971 was the first generation that shared basic structure with Cedric after Nissan merged with Prince in 1966. Its elegant and graceful styling of moderately adopted coke bottle line gained very favorable reviews. Japan's first pillarless 4-door hardtop that had both beautiful styling and comfortability was added in 1972, which created a trend of domestic high-end cars for the following several decades. 230 sedan was often seen in police dramas televised years ago in Japan. This car is Custom Deluxe Sedan with L20 engine. Other equipment includes 4-speed column shift, trunk lid opener of vacuum type, seat belts with automatic locking retractor mechanism (ALR) and intermittent wipers.

Starting with the 230 launched in February 1971, the Cedric and Gloria were integrated into one model. The Cedric and Gloria then differed only in the hood panel/mascot, radiator grille and rear combination lamps and finisher, etc. In April of the same year, a 4-door hardtop version (without center pillar) was introduced, Japan's first in the 2-liter class. Following a minor change in April 1973, the Custom Deluxe was fitted with a heated rear window as standard.

The second-generation Laurel (C130) was launched in April 1972. The sophisticated styling proved very popular. Starting with this model, the Laurel had a 2-liter L20 engine instead of G18 and G20; in October 1973, the 2.6 liter (L26) version was also included in the lineup. The SGX (L20 only) boasted a high output of 130PS (regular gasoline engine was 125PS) with its SU twin-carb engine.

model_full: New Silvia LS Type S (1975: S10)
description: The first generation Silvia released in 1965 was a high-end 2-seater sports coupe, but the second generation S10 released in 1975 fell into the specialty car category. The hardtop body with spaceship-like styling attracted attention. Features included deep-set headlamps and front grill, combination rear lamps and side character line that went down to rear wheel arch. Exterior was such characteristic, but interior was sporty with horizontally aligned 4 round meters. Originally Nissan's first rotary engine was to be mounted but the plan was canceled due to oil crisis, etc. Actually mounted was L18 engine (4-cyl.in line OHC, 1800cc). The official name of S10 series is "New Silvia" in Japan, while "Datsun 200SX" in the U.S.

model_full: Cherry FII Coupe Coupe GX-Twin (1976 : KPF10)
description: Cherry, Nissan's first FWD (front wheel drive) car, evolved into the second generation "Cherry F-II" (F10) at full-model change in 1974. This machine was produced for catalog on the base of the top grade car "GX Twin" on which an engine with twin carburetors was mounted. Its engine was enhanced to 145ps and was manufactured in compliance with regulations of TS races at the time. In Japan, unfortunately it was only an exhibit and didn't run at any races since Nissan had decided not to participate in races. But it actually ran and won at a race as a proof of high potential in New Zealand. This car is yellow because of the copy "Yellow Cherry" at release.

The fifth generation Bluebird 810 was a successor of 610 and was released in 1976. There were many problems to solve at the time such as exhaust emission (environmental problems), oil crisis (fuel consumption problems) and cutting down on traffic fatalities (safety problems). Therefore, efforts had to be poured into developing countermeasures such as Electronically Controlled Gas Injection, NAPS (Nissan Anti-Pollution System) and seat belts with ELR (emergency locking retractor). As a result, Bluebird had to become less sporty. But, without overcoming these difficulties, automobiles might have disappeared by now. This car is Sports Sedan 1800 SSS-E·S of the highest grade.

The fourth generation Skyline C110 was rolled out in September 1972, but it was required at that time that all the cars of existing models and new models should conform the emission regulations that became increasingly rigor. Due to this situation, Nissan stopped the works activities of Skyline 2000GT-R in touring car races and the development resources had to concentrate on cleaner emission. The main engine of Skyline series was the inline 6-cylinder OHC "L20" of 1,998cc, but it was changed from the traditional carburetor system to "L20E" of the EGI (Electronic Gasoline Injection) system. This car is the upper-grade 2000GTX-E with L20E engine. C110 series sold more than 660 thousand units that was the best sales results among the Skyline generations, owing to the successful marketing campaign of "Skyline for Ken and Mary."

The fourth-generation Cedric, the 330, was launched in June 1975. Both a sedan and hardtop (2-door/4-door) versions were available. The dignified styling was very popular. Following a minor change in June 1977, it became the 331, and the 2800 Brougham was introduced. This car, along with a Bluebird, was used for newsgathering along the Asian Highway (Route A1) by the Asahi Newspaper Co..

The fifth-generation Bluebird, the 810, was introduced in July 1976. The lineup included 1,600cc, 1,800cc and 2,000cc versions. Then in 1978, there was a minor change in the design to create the 811 with its square headlights. This car was used together with a Cedric (commemorative car #076) by the team compiling the Asahi newspaper's serialized reports on Route A1 of the Asian Highway network.

The first-generation Fairlady Z (S30) was announced in October 1969 and launched in November that same year. In Japan, the 240Z was launched two years later in November 1971, followed by the 2/2 model in January 1974. In July 1976, this car evolved into the S31 (1976 "NAPS"=Nissan Anti-Pollution System= spec.). This Z-T (5-speed, floor shift only) was equipped with aluminum wheels, 195/70HR14 tires, and remote-controlled mirrors as standard.

The first generation Fairlady Z (S30) was born in 1969 as a successor of convertible sports car Datsun Fairlady and became a global big hit. Mounted engines were L20 (6-cyl.in line OHC, 2000cc, SU type twin carburetors) and S20 (6-cyl.in line 4-valve DOHC, 2000cc, SOLEX twin-choke triple carburetors). S20 was discontinued in 1973 due to the emission control. L20 was revised by changing SU type twin carburetors to electronically controlled fuel injection system and became L20E to comply with the emission control in 1976. The model became S31. This car is S31 Z-T manufactured in 1977.

The first Violet (Datsun 710) appeared in January 1973. Two types of engines, the L14 and the L16, were used and the lineup included a sedan and hardtop. It performed well in overseas rallies. This commemorative car won the 12th Southern Cross Rally (Australia) in 1977. It is powered by a rally-use twin-cam, 16-valve engine.

The fourth generation Cedric 330 was released in 1975. The lineup was the same as that of favored 230; 4-door sedan, 2-door/4-door hardtop and van, but the styling became more intricate. It cleared the exhaust emission regulations in 1975 by NAPS (Nissan Anti Pollution System). The model 331 was released in 1976 to comply with the regulations of that year and 332 was released in 1978 to comply with the regulations of that year. Sedan with diesel engine of 2200cc was added in 1977, which suggested the potential for the age of diesel engines. The model 330 as well as 230 could be seen in police dramas televised years ago. This is Cedric 2000 Deluxe Sedan (332).

After the oil shock, the fifth-generation 810, which appeared in July 1976, was designed to be a safe, economical, low-consumption car. The 811 represented a minor change. In August 1978, it was launched as the '78 NAPS specification model. The 811, with the 2x2 square headlights giving it a bold appearance, was given a new catchphrase for TV commercials: "The heavy-duty choice".

A second-generation Z (S130), equipped with a 6-cylinder in line 2,758cc L28 engine was launched in August 1978 as the 280Z. Attracting interest was the new styling, which featured the traditional long nose and short deck, blended with sharper lines, while the grille-less front end enhanced the unified look of the body. Both the 2-seater and the 2/2 offered more spacious interiors, further improving comfort.

The second generation Patrol 60 remained a long-selling product from 1960 to 1980 when the next generation Safari 160 was released. Robust design of ladder frame and leaf rigid suspension was passed down from the first generation 4W60. 2WD and 4WD could be switched by a lever. The lineup had short body (the wheelbase of 2200mm), long body (the wheelbase of 2500mm), soft top/hard top/van/station wagon. It is also adopted as fire engine (with the wheelbase of 2800mm) because of its powerful engine and mobility. In overseas markets, the name Patrol has been passed down since the first generation that was born in 1951. This is the most long-lasting name except "Nissan/Datsun Pickup". This car is its fire engine version that worked in a company for 37 years from 1978 to 2005.

The A10, which made its overseas debut in the spring of 1978 at the Safari Rally (3rd overall), won the autumn Southern Cross Rally in Australia two years in a row (in 1977 it was the 710). The driver was the previous year's Australian champion, J. Fury. In Australia the car was sold as the Stanza, so a "STANZA" emblem adorns the body.

The first generation Caravan, also known as "Urvan" E20 rolled out in 1973 was a multi-purpose commercial van of the cab over type. "Chaircab" was added in 1977 that had a lift and an anchoring device for a wheelchair. A long-run charity TV program in Japan started in 1978 with the watchwords of "Welfare", "Environment", and "Disaster Recovery". Nissan, as a major sponsor, has donated many welfare vehicles from the beginning of the program. This is the actual car of No.27 among 213 donated welfare cars in 1978 and was used at a welfare facility for about 20 years. The logo of the program is drawn on the body. It was restored by Autech Japan, Inc. in 2015 to the almost brand-new condition including the electric lift.

The fourth generation Sunny B310 was rolled out in 1977 when automobiles were blamed as a cause of air pollution. Besides improving overall performance, meeting emission control regulations in 1978 was the problem. Nissan developed an exhaust purification system "NAPS: Nissan Anti-Pollution System" to meet the strict regulations. Fuel consumption was improved to 15.5km/l in the 10-mode test for 1200cc car. 1400cc cars with EGI (electronic fuel injection system) were added in 1978. B310 was the last DATSUN Sunny and also the last rear-driven Sunny with smooth handling. 5-door station wagon "Sunny California" added in 1979 became a topic car of a new type with usability.

The Bluebird 910 launch was in November 1979. Thanks in part to its straight-line styling and high-quality build, it achieved the tremendous record of being the top seller for 27 consecutive months (from the month after its launch to February 1982) in the compact vehicle class. All of the engines (1,600cc, 1,800cc and 2,000cc) were now 4-cylinder models. The improved drive stability that came from the zero-scrub suspension was widely noticed.
NA

Laurel opened the personally-owned car market in Japan when it was rolled out in 1968. The third generation in 1977 was a model designed on the concept of "a sophisticated, stately, luxurious, and fashionable car for owners of upper class". The lineup was traditional 2-door hardtop and 4-door sedan, and "4-door hardtop" with no B pillars. This "4-door hardtop" is a body structure first introduced in Japan for NISSAN "Cedric / Gloria" in 1972. It became a popular category that realized beautiful form, sense of openness, comfortableness, and utility, and created a trend in the personally-owned car market in Japan that lasted for decades. This is a 2-door hardtop SGL-E in elegant copper brown.

The fifth generation Skyline C210 was released in 1977. Unlike the fourth generation C110 "Skyline for Ken and Mary" with laid-back form, C210 had a sharp styling that was reminiscent of the third generation C10 "Ai-no-Skyline (Skyline Of Love)". It has a nickname "Japan" that came from the copy "Skyline Japan", meaning a great car cultivated in Japan. It was remodeled to C211 to comply with the emission control regulations in 1978. Performance improvement was pausing at the time because of increasing rigor of emission control. It was the most difficult time for Skyline. This car is 2000 GT-E·L with EGI engine of 130ps. The model was C211 of the early days manufactured in 1979.

This car was the overall winner (S. Mehta/M. Doughty) of the 27th Safari Rally (1979), the Nissan team's fourth Safari championship victory after a gap of six years. The competition was strong in that year's Safari - with the Mercedes Benz 450SLC, Peugeot 504, and Abarth 131 - but Nissan fought bravely, taking 1st, 5th, 7th and 9th places. The official entry name was "Datsun 160J".

430 rolled out in 1979 as the fifth generation Cedric and the sixth generation Gloria had a linear, clean form and got favorable reviews. Japan's first Electronic Concentrated Engine Control System (ECCS) was implemented in the model with 2800cc engine to control ignition and idling by computer. Today, it is considered as the very first step toward "intelligent vehicles". Japan's first turbo engine (L20E·T) cars were added in 1979, which triggered the trend for turbo engines since they enable small displacement engine to achieve high power and good fuel efficiency. 430 was often seen in police dramas televised years ago. This car is Cedric 4-door Sedan 200E SGL Extra, fully restored in 2019 by Autech Japan, Inc.

The sixth-generation Gloria (430) was launched in June 1979. The styling was modified to emphasize straight lines. With the appearance of this model, the 2-door hardtop version was discontinued. In October that year, the first domestic model to be fitted with a turbo engine was introduced. It underwent minor changes in April 1981 and in June 1982.

The Junior was a medium-size vehicle introduced to fill the gap between the Datsun and Nissan trucks. The first-generation B40 was launched in October 1956. Later, due to a change in the compact- vehicle standard, the newly designed model 40 was introduced in 1960. The 140, which integrated the Junior and Miler, was introduced in 1970 and in 1974, an improved model, the 141 (conforming to 1975 exhaust emission regulations), was launched.

The design concept of the third-generation Laurel (C230), launched in January 1977, focused on safety, low emissions, and low consumption. Its distinguishing feature was its styling, with its well-rounded bodylines and large central grille. A new 4-door hardtop version was also introduced. The C231, launched in November 1980, conformed to 1978 exhaust emission regulations.

model: Nissan Cedric 4-door Hardtop Turbo SGL Extra
model_full: Nissan Cedric 4-door Hardtop Turbo SGL Extra (1980: 430)
description: 430 was rolled out as the fifth generation Cedric and the sixth generation Gloria in 1979. Unlike the preceding 2 generations, it had a linear form that got favorable reviews. Japan's first Electronic Concentrated Engine Control System (ECCS) was adopted to control ignition and idling, to power up, and to improve fuel efficiency and environmental performance. Turbo engine (L20E·T) cars were added in 1979 during the second oil crisis. Since turbocharger technologies enable small displacement engine to achieve high power and fuel efficiency, turbo engines met the demand for energy saving and Nissan triggered the trend. This car is Cedric Turbo SGL Extra 4-door Hardtop.

As Nissan's flagship car, this high-quality sedan boasted the best in technology and luxury. The H252 indicates that it was derived from the Cedric Special (50), launched in August 1963. The 250 was launched in 1973, and the 252, which conformed to 1978 exhaust emission regulations, was launched in August 1977. The top-grade Sovereign was equipped with an 4,400cc V8 engine.

The first generation Pulsar N10 was rolled out in 1978 as successor to the second generation Cherry F10. Pulsar aimed at "high quality car of international level" with performance enough to compete in European market full of great compact cars, and evolved into a car with more comfortableness, more safety, and more functionality. The form with verve is also impressive. The advertisement "Pulsar Europe" in which rival cars such as VW Golf and Renault 5 appeared reflected that spirit and became a topic. The lineup was 4-door sedan, 3-door 2-box hatchback, 3-door coupe with glass hatch, and commercial van. This is Sedan 1200TS in 1980, restored by Autech Japan Inc. in 2020.

The C210, which was the fifth-generation Skyline, was launched in 1977. It was popular for its straight bodylines. The C211 was introduced in 1980 following a minor change. Three versions of 2000GT were available: Turbo GT-E (145PS), GT-E (125PS), and the GT (115PS). This 2000GT was donated by Teshima, who used it to drive right round Australia.

The fifth-generation Skyline (nickname: "Japan") was launched in August 1977. All the cars in the series met the 1978 exhaust emission regulations, and the new TI-EX model featured halogen headlights. The GT family included GT, GT-L, GT-EL, GT-EX, and GT-ES models. A minor change in 1979 changed the front mask, and another in 1980 introduced the turbo GT-E.

The launch in May 1977 of the second-generation Violet (A10) completed the trio: Violet (Nissan), Auster (Cherry) and Stanza (Sunny). Inheriting Nissan's rally tradition, the A10 did well in the overseas rallies, like the 710 Violet. This commemorative car was driven by S. Mehta team when they won the 28th Safari Rally in 1980.

The sixth generation Bluebird 910 rolled out in 1979 was an epoch-making car with a linear form of 510, retrieved high traveling performance and pioneering technologies. Technological topics were enlarged tread and overall width, 4-cylinder engine variations, front suspension setting called zero-scrub radius geometry, rack & pinion steering gear, etc. The square body styling also improved roominess and comfortability. 910 refreshed the image of Bluebird and became a big hit. It was the top selling car in the category of 1600-2000cc passenger vehicles for 27 months in Japan. This car is 2000SSS-EX of 1981 with Z20E engine (120ps, 2 spark plugs for each cylinder), and "7-way seat" that has 7 adjustment functions.

Fairlady rolled out in 1969 became a worldwide hit, which was unusual for sports cars. In 1978, it evolved into the second generation S130 after the first full model change. Lineup in Japan was "Z" (2000cc, 6-cyl. inline, OHC) and "280Z" (2800cc). It was known as "DATSUN 280ZX" in overseas markets. This car is Fairlady 280Z-T 2by2 in 1981 of the highest grade. Mounted engine was L28E (max. output 155ps), and air conditioner, power window, and aluminum wheels were equipped as standard. The specialized car "SUPER Z" in a police dramas televised years ago was manufactured based on 280Z. SUPER Z was a legendary machine with gull-wing doors and varius special equipment.

The Gazelle (hardtop) was launched in March 1979 as a sibling to the third-generation Silvia. Designed to be a specialty car, the S110 was distinguished by its refined styling and electronics. In August of the same year, the hatchback series was added to the lineup, and in May 1981 a powerful turbo version was launched.

The fourth generation Laurel C31 made a debut in 1980. The concept was "vehicles with advanced performance and global awareness for owners of upper class in 1980s". It got favorable reviews for sleek aerodynamic form and high basic performance. It featured a low waistline, large windows, and the low center-of-gravity. 4-door hardtop model achieved the outstanding drag coefficient (Cd) of 0.38. The idea that the basic performance of "run, turn, stop" is important even for luxury cars was a belief of S. Sakurai, the chief engineer of C31. The idea still stands in Nissan. This is a high-grade model "2000 Turbo SGX" with "L20E·T" turbo engine (6-cyl., 145ps, 2000cc).

The sixth-generation Skyline (Type R30), was launched in August 1981. For the advertising campaign, the actor Paul Newman - a familiar face in racing circles - was hired, and the catchphrase "New Love Skyline" attracted much attention. The 6-cylinder and 4-cylinder models used bodies with the same nose length. A 5-door hatchback was also launched, while the estate wagon was discontinued.

With the 29th Safari Rally in 1981, this vehicle achieved a historical first by winning three championships in a row (a first too for the S. Mehta/M. Doughty). That year, in addition to a pair of Violets prepared to Group 4 specifications with powerful twin-cam heads, the Nissan team entered a Violet, Bluebird and Silvia, each prepared to Group 2 specifications. The result was that Nissan monopolized the top four places.

With the 430, launched in June 1979, there was no 2-door hardtop version but the estate wagon was reintroduced. This was Nissan's first model to adopt the Engine Central Control System (ECCS). Following a minor change in December 1979, Japan's first car with a turbo engine was introduced and new technology that improved the fuel economy of the turbo won high praise.

model_full: Datsun Bluebird 4H/T 1800 Turbo SSS-E/ G (1982 : KP910)
description: Launched in November 1979, the 910 (sixth-generation model) was the last Bluebird to bear the Datsun name. With its straight bodylines and the sporty ride offered by the newly developed zero-scrub suspension, it proved very popular. It was the best selling car (compact car category) for 27 months in a row. The SSS-E/G was the top-grade model, equipped with a multi-voice warning system.

The first-generation Leopard (F30), designed to be a specialty car, was launched in September 1980. This well-appointed hardtop was available in both 4-door and 2-door versions, with a choice of two engines: the 2,000cc L20 or the 2,800cc L28. There was a minor change in 1982, when it was equipped with the world's first steering switches by optical communications.

The first generation March K10 was rolled out in 1982. The image character was a popular singer/actor Masahiko "Matchy" Kondo and the model became very popular due to appealing copies such as "Matchy's March" and "Super Idol". This car is one and only special machine with a similar appearance to that of racing machines of "Super Silhouette (Group 5)". It was manufactured for M. Kondo who was known as a car lover and wanted to be a racing driver. Mounted engine of E15 (1500cc, OHC) was tuned up to 160ps. The impressive body riveted people's attention. M. Kondo practiced driving technique for motor sports on this car around 1983 and started a career as a racing driver.

The third generation Silvia S110 released in 1979 and its variation car Gazelle were closely connected with motor sports such as Super Silhouette Races and WRC. This is 240RS that was developed based on S110 as Group B rally car to participate in WRC, and the number of produced units was more than 200. Markets were mainly overseas and many of them were left-hand drive cars. FJ24 engine (4-valve DOHC, 2340cc) generated 240ps in the standard specs and FJ24rev. for works machines generated as much as 275ps. The best achievement was the second-place finish at Rally New Zealand in 1983. This car was restored to the state at the debut race by Nissan Restoration Club in 2006.

Fairlady Z, unusual for sports car, became a global hit when it was rolled out in 1969. It was evolved into the second generation S130 at a full-model change in 1978. Lineup in Japan was "Z" with 6-cyl. inline OHC, 2000cc engine and "280Z" with 2800cc engine. It is known as "DATSUN 280ZX" in overseas. This is two-seater 280Z with Japan's first "T-top" that built a sense of openness. Since T-top structure provided much more rigidity of body than fully openable roof, could meet severe collision safety standards, and required no big modification of body structure, it became prevalent in US in 1980s. This car is specially colored in black and silver.

The fourth-generation Laurel C31 Series released in 1980 was a luxury sedan with aerodynamic styling and high basic performance. From 1981 the world-renowned fashion designer Hubert de Givenchy served as the image character, and furthermore in 1982, a limited release of 500 "Givenchy version" cars was made in collaboration with the Givenchy brand. The car here is the favorite car of Shotaro Shimomura, the 12th generation head of the Shimomura family known for founding the Daimaru department store chain. The car has a piece of trivia related to it, for on the occasion of the 30-year Givenchy retrospective in 1983, Givenchy himself, who was a close friend of Shimomura, and the actor Audrey Hepburn, who was visiting Japan for the first time, rode in the car between Itami Airport and the Shimomura residence (Daimaru Villa in Kyoto). After the owner passed, it was preserved in the garage of the Daimaru Villa, and in 2022, it was generously donated to Nissan Heritage Collection.

model_full: Nissan Silvia Coupe Turbo ZSE-X (1982: S110)
description: "Silvia" is a Nissan's leading specialty car. The third generation S110 and its sibling car Gazelle were rolled out at the same time in 1979. 2-door hardtop with square 4-bulb headlights was added in March, and 3-door hatchback with "Z-car"-like large tailgate in August. Lineup was expanded later by adding "RS" that shared FJ20E engine (4-valve DOHC) with "Skyline RS", and models with Z18E·T turbo engines. As was typical in 1980s, it was equipped with many futuristic technologies such as digital meters, drive assist computer almost as functional as rally computers, voice information, and world's first sound recognition power windows. This is Turbo ZSE-X in 1982.

The third-generation Silvia, the S110, was launched in March 1979 and the RS version, with the FJ20 engine, was launched in April 1982.Overseas, the export-specification rally car (LZ20B engine) performed well in the Safari Rally as the successor to the Violet (PA10). It was 3rd overall in the 1982 Safari Rally.

Rear-wheel drive cars transitioned to front-wheel drive (FWD) cars in the first half of 1980s for higher space efficiency and most of them adopted FWD with "transverse engine layout". The Nissan's first FWD car was "Cherry" in 1970. The fifth generation Sunny B11 in 1981 was the third product line of FWD car after "Pulsar" and "Violet Liberta". Mounted engine was mainly E (1300cc and 1500cc, 4 cylinders) developed for FWD. Lineup was sedan, 3-door, and 5-door wagon (named "California"). This car is 1500cc sedan, the best-selling model at the time. This generation was the first model that was sold in US market as NISSAN Sentra. Annual output of B11 in 1983 was the largest among world top-selling models like VW Golf and Toyota Corolla.
NA

This is the car that won the 30th Safari Rally in the overall category in 1982 by exerting its high travelling performance and high reliability. That was the unprecedented 4th straight victory for both NISSAN and S. Mehta, the driver, and M. Doughty, the navigator, which made the headlines. The mounted engine was "LZ20B" with the in line 4-cyl DOHC, the displacement of 1,975cc, and the max. power of 230ps as was specified by the Group 4 rules. Although Violet Model PA10 had a well-balanced chassis and an engine that had both high power and endurance, it retired as a rally car with the glittering record because rules on vehicles of Groups 2 and 4 terminated in that year. In 2009, "NISSAN Restoration Club" fully restored it, while keeping damages as they are, to hand down the car to the next generation.

Despite retaining the form of the production car, this monster machine is a "Super Silhouette," a race category introduced into Japan in 1979. Driven by H. Yanagida, this Bluebird won the championship title twice, in 1980 and 1982. In the 1983 Fuji GC series, it won 3 rounds out of 4. It also won the Tsukuba event, displaying overwhelming power.

The first-generation Laurel, the C30, was launched in April 1968. Following two full model changes in April 1972 and January 1977, the fourth-generation model, the C31, was launched on November 5, 1980. The C31 was distinguished by its simple and clean styling. Its slanted nose and low hood gave the C31 superior aerodynamics (Cd: 0.38). It was the first Laurel to be equipped with a turbocharger and Engine Central Control System (ECCS), and it also offered several features to improve cabin comfort: an improved suspension, a roomier interior, auto-levelizer (a device to maintain vehicle height automatically), Japan's first automatic seat-setter with a seat lifter that can adjust steplessly, computer-controlled automatic air conditioner, and high-quality audio system. Eight engines were available: the 4-cylinder Z18 and Z20; the 6-cylinder L20, L20E, L20ET and L28E; and the diesel LD20 and LD28. Also, the wide range of basic model types included 38 sedans and 20 hardtops. Top of the line was the Medalist, powered by either a 2,000cc or 2,800cc gasoline engine and equipped with an auto-levelizer, computer-controlled automatic air conditioner, high-quality audio system, and ASCD (Automatic Speed Control Device) as standard.

The accumulated production of "Fairlady" series since DATSUN Fairlady SPL212/213 in 1960 reached one million in 1983 when the third generation Fairlady Z (Z31) was rolled out. Its newly developed compact "VG" engine (V6, 2000cc and 3000cc) was a hot topic. Weight balance of entire vehicle was improved, which resulted in drastic improvement of traveling performance. The edgy form with traditional long nose/short deck and drag coefficient (Cd)=0.31 features semi-retractable headlights, called "Parallel Rising Headlamps". This is "NISSAN 300ZX Turbo" with VG30ET engine. It is of Canadian spec. and also of special edition on Nissan Motor's 50th anniversary in 1983.

This is the machine driven by K. Hoshino at the Fuji Super Silhouette races (held between 1979 and 1984). Super Silhouette cars looked like production cars outside, but sported Formula car engineering inside. In accordance with international Group 5 regulations, the engine was the same twin-carb LZ20B (570PS) used in the Skyline Super Silhouette.

The sixth generation Skyline R30 released in 1981 was called “Newman Skyline” because the image character was Paul Newman, a Hollywood star and racing driver. FJ20E engine (4-cyl. 4-valve DOHC) mounted on 2000RS became very popular as the first DOHC engine on Skyline in eight years. 2000 Turbo RS was added in 1983 with FJ20E･T (190ps) engine that was a combination of FJ20E and turbo. The engine was so powerful that the car was called “The most powerful Skyline in history”. The front grille was removed at the minor change in August 1983 and so RS series cars was nicknamed “Iron mask” because of unique front end without grille. This car is 2000 Turbo RS of the early spec

The 6th generation Skyline R30 released in 1981 was called "Newman Skyline" because Paul Newman, an actor and racing driver, appeared as a poster boy. A new face "2000 RS" with "FJ20" engine of 4-cyl. 4-valve DOHC became very popular along with 2000GT Turbo since the 5th generation. "Turbo RS" with turbo-charged FJ20 engine made a debut in 1983. Its max. output was 190ps which was the highest of all the Skyline cars in generations. Although its sales copy was "Most powerful Skyline ever," it didn't proclaim itself "GT-R." This car is "2000 Turbo RS" with horizontal grills in the earlier days. The model was used in very popular police dramas televised in Japan in 1980s.
NA

In the Super Silhouette races that started in 1979, Masahiro Hasemi competed in the 1982 and 1983 seasons driving this machine. The category allowed heavy modifications and this monster, although the same as a production car on the outside, is the equivalent of a Formula racing car on the inside. Its dynamic performance won many fans. The engine is a LZ20B turbo (570PS). Its race debut was in May 1982 and it did extremely well, chalking up 2 wins in 1982 and 5 wins in 1983.

Since the appearance of the first-generation model 30 (announced in March 1960, launched in April), the Cedric - noted for its impressive styling and advanced automotive technologies - has stood at the forefront of Japanese automobile manufacture, demonstrating consistent popularity in a broad range of applications, from personal to formal. The sixth-generation model Y30 was launched on June 22, 1983. This model attracted a great deal of interest as Japan's first passenger car to be powered by a V-type 6-cylinder OHC engine. Its distinctive styling featured a dignified front grille design and a stable, low-profile silhouette. The 4-door hardtop, 4-door sedan, station wagon and van all received high praise. Three versions of the newly developed VG engine were available for the Y30: the VG30E (180PS), VG20E (130PS), and VG20ET (170PS). New engine noise suppression, a lengthened wheelbase (+40mm), double vibration proofing for the suspension, and flush body surfaces all contributed to ensuring a quiet and comfortable interior. In addition to the VG engine, 3 other engines were available: the economical LD28 (6-cylinder in-line diesel), CA20S (4-cylinder in-line gasoline, available for the sedan & van), and CA20P (LPG, available for the sedan). These engines were mainly used for the sedan since it is the first choice for formal (limousine/taxi) applications. Two engines were available for limousine rental specifications: the LD28 (diesel) and CA20P (LPG).

model: Nissan Laurel 4-door Hardtop Turbo Medalist Eminence
model_full: Nissan Laurel 4-door Hardtop Turbo Medalist Eminence (1984: GC32)
description: Laurel was a groundbreaking product rolled in 1968 that created unprecedented "personal luxury car for owners of upper class" market. The fifth generation C32 was developed on the concept of "most luxurious saloon that appeals to sensibility of the driver" and rolled out in 1984. Advanced technologies adopted included world's first "power-folding door mirror", world's first "automatic glare-proof rearview mirror", and raindrop sensing automatic wiper. Newly-developed "RB" engine (6-cyl. inline) was one of the topics. This is V20 Turbo Medalist Eminence with VG20E·T engine, the top-of-the-line model with power-folding door mirror and automatic wiper equipped as standard.

The first-generation Prairie was a pioneer in the multipurpose RV market, which eventually led to today's popular minivans. It was launched in August 1982. Thanks to its FF design, it offered two sliding side doors on both sides, without the obstruction of a central pillar, something not seen on any other passenger vehicle at the time. This made getting in and out much easier. The JW-G was an 8-seater; a 5-seater and 3/6-seater were also available.

Launched in 1982, this is the racing version of the second-generation Pulsar. A normal engine was used for the normal car races. To adapt it for circuit racing, the suspension was strengthened and equipment such as a roll bar, extinguisher, and kill switch were installed to meet safety regulations. The base vehicle was the 3-door hatchback Milano X-1 (launched in March 1984).

As with No. 101 above, the Milano X-1(launched in March 1984) was used as the basis for this racing version. It performed well in national rookie races (normal car races), such as the Fuji Freshman Race. The engine is normal, but the suspension was strengthened and safety equipment required for racing - such as the roll bar and extinguisher - added.

The sixth generation Skyline R30 rolled out in 1981 is called "Newman Skyline" since the image character was an actor/racing driver Paul Newman. "2000RS" series with "FJ20" engine (4-cyl. 4-valve, DOHC), as well as 2000GT turbo series, won popularity. " Turbo RS" with FJ20 turbo engine was added in 1983. " The Most Powerful Skyline" was the copy since its max. output reached 190ps, the highest among all the Skyline models. RS series underwent a minor change in 1983 to have a unique front mask without front grille and was called "Iron Mask". Turbo RS became "Turbo Intercooler RS" with the output of 205ps in 1984. This car is "Turbo Intercooler RS·X" of the higher grade.

model: Cedric 4-door Hardtop V30 Turbo Brougham VIP
model_full: Cedric 4-door Hardtop V30 Turbo Brougham VIP (1985 : PY30)
description: Since the first-generation model (30) appeared in April 1960, the Cedric has been at the forefront of the luxury sedan market, a domestically manufactured passenger car that truly represents Japan. The sixth-generation Y30 was launched on June 22, 1983. Attracting attention as the first Japanese passenger car with a V6 engine (VG30E/VG20E), the Y30 also featured a wealth of advanced electronic technologies, including the world's first automatic windshield wiper system with rain sensor and intermittent mode, electronic radio tuner (turbo models) with track display and program reservation, illuminated (EL) hood mascot, and computer-controlled fully automatic air conditioner. On January 9, 1984, the V30E Brougham VIP debuted as the top-of-the-line model, complete with such standard equipment as computer-controlled power seats (position memory for all 4 seats). And on June 18 of that year the lineup gained two new models, the Turbo Brougham VIP and Turbo Brougham, both powered by the same turbocharged VG30ET engine (max. output: 230PS) used on the Fairlady Z. The V30 Turbo Brougham VIP had improved suspension and brakes, and came with such standard equipment as an auto-levelizer to maintain vehicle height, and computer-controlled power seats. The wide range of options included genuine leather seats, keyless entry system, JBL speaker system, and fiber-optic steering wheel switches.

model_full: DATSUN Pickup Long Body Deluxe (1985: CG720)
description: Nissan's commercial vehicle "DATSUN Truck (Pickup)" has been on the market since early days of the company and now it's known as "NISSAN NP300 Navara" in the global market. 720 rolled out in 1979 had a linear and sharp form like Silvia S110 (200SX in US) that was on the market at the time. Introduction of the first 4WD model to lineup to respond to increasing demand for recreation use was a big turning point. Production of the model started at Nissan Motor Manufacturing Corp. (current Nissan North America Inc.) in Smyrna, Tennessee in 1983 to meet the demand for pickup trucks in US. This is" Flat Bed Long body Deluxe" with Z16 engine after a minor change in 1982.

The EV Guide (type II) was exhibited at the 26th Tokyo Motor Show in 1985 and is a one-box type, six-seater electric car (remodeled after the show to add a roof). The clean performance of this electric car made it ideal for transporting royalty and other state guests on VIP factory visits, and it performed admirably as a guide car for many years.

The third-generation Z (Z31) was launched in 1983, the same year as the Fairlady production total passed 1 million units. Unlike the 2.8-liter, the 3.0-liter model was the first in Japan to use a V6 turbo engine and attracted much interest. Its beautiful silhouette, boasting a drag coefficient (Cd) of 0.31, and its unique parallel-rising headlights were very popular.

model: Fairlady Z 300ZX, Japanese Rally Championship in 1985
model_full: Fairlady Z 300ZX, Japanese Rally Championship in 1985 (1985 : HZ31)
description: Japan's world famous sportscar Fairlady Z evolved into the third generation Z31 in 1983. Its sharp styling with traditional long nose and short rear deck made a vivid impression. The hottest topic was newly designed turbo engine of V6 (only 2000cc and 3000cc in early days). V6 engine that was more compact than inline engine improved weight distribution and drastically improved dynamic performance. This car is "300ZX" of rally spec with VG30ET engine (3000cc, 230ps). At Japanese Rally Championship in 1985, this machine showed stable performance in each round, won first place in the 6th and 7th rounds, and finally won the series championship.

The first-generation Leopard (F30), with its innovative styling and advanced technologies, was presented as a "new genre, new age car", providing high performance and high quality. It was launched on September 30, 1980 with its sibling, the Leopard TR-X (F30Y). The F30's styling was instantly recognizable: it combined smooth curves and sharp lines to create a dynamic, streamlined form. It also featured a slanted nose with headlights set at 26.5 degrees (the highest angle for a domestic model) and sharply slanted windshield, giving it excellent aerodynamic performance (Cd: 0.37). The interior was distinguished by its elegant soft-trim finish, used throughout the cabin. The F30 was equipped with the world's first electronic multi-meter, a drive computer, an audio system with auto-volume control (the first of its type in a Japanese car), tilting/telescopic steering column, and automatic air conditioner (standard equipment for the top-of-the-line model). Nissan also adopted several advanced technologies to ensure a comfortable ride - zero-scrub suspension, ventilated disc brakes (all models), and Japan's first auto-levelizer (standard equipment on the top-grade SF-L). To start with, there was a choice of 2 series, the 4-door hardtop and 2-door hardtop, plus 3 engines: the L28E, L20E, and Z18S. On July 28 of the following year, the L20E turbo engine was added to the lineup. Also, on the September 20, 1982, following a minor change, the front grille was changed to a transparent plastic type. Launched at that time, the 200XZGX was the top of the non-turbo line, equipped with the world's first fiber-optic steering wheel switches (ASCD and audio switches mounted in the center pad), and high-quality plain-weave cloth upholstery as standard.

The first-generation March (K10) was launched in October 1982. In April 1983, the fashionable, high-quality "Collet" was added to the lineup (based on the top grade G). Chic and luxurious, the Collet proved very popular with the young crowd and women. In February 1985, the first minor change was carried out.

This machine took part in the GTP Series of the US IMSA GT Championship. In 1988 G. Brabham won the Driver's Championship in it. The V6 engine is a modified VG30ET. California-based Electramotive Engineering was responsible for developing and racing the vehicle, winning the Constructor's Championship in 1989, 1990 and 1991.

model: Nissan Safari 4WD Hardtop Standard roof AD
model_full: Nissan Safari 4WD Hardtop Standard roof AD (1985 : VR161)
description: The first generation "Patrol" was rolled out in 1951. In Japan, it became "Safari" when the third generation 160 was rolled out in 1980. In overseas countries, it continues to be Patrol, a time-proven brand with the robust frame and reliable rigid suspension with leaf springs. 160 had user-friendly equipment and interior to enhance passengers' comfort to satisfy the demand for 4WD cars for recreation. Safari in Japan started with SD33 engine (3300cc, 95ps, diesel) and evolved into 161 in 1983 that featured SD33T engine (120ps, diesel with turbo) and 5-speed manual transmission. High roof van type model was also added to lineup. This is the car of "AD" (adventure) grade in 1985.

model: Nissan Skyline GT Twin-cam 24V Turbo Passage
model_full: Nissan Skyline GT Twin-cam 24V Turbo Passage (1985: HR31)
description: Known as "Seventh", the R31 Skyline appeared in 1985 with full model change. The upper-grade model introduced many new features: newly developed RB20DE (165ps) straight-six engine with 4-valve DOHC, its turbocharged version RB20DET (210ps), and "HICAS", the first suspension that allows the rear wheels to form angles according to lateral gravity and speed. Additionally, it was the first model with "Card Entry System" which was the origin of the today's "Intelligent Key". This "Passage Twin Cam 24V Turbo" was the fastest model at the time of its debut. Later in 1986, the long-awaited two-door coupe was released. The coupe model played an active part in touring car races.

Pulsar EXA rolled out in 1982 is a coupe model of Pulsar. The daring form with slanting retractable headlights was designed to pursue an image totally different from that of Pulsar sedan or hatchback. One-make race was held for EXA, a compact sporty model. This "Convertible" was rolled out in 1985 as a commemorative car of 15th anniversary of dealers of NISSAN Cherry. The number of production was only 100. This car is manufactured based on EXA 5-speed MT. The soft-top is made of specially woven cloth with high weatherproof and waterproof performance and organic glass of polycarbonate series is adopted for better rearward visibility.

The seventh-generation Skyline (R31), commonly known as the "Seven", was launched in August 1985. With this model, the 6-cylinder DOHC was reintroduced and in autumn that same year, a race-specification machine was exhibited at the Tokyo Motor Show, where it attracted longing looks from visitors. From 1986 it competed in the All Japan Championship, in which driver A. Suzuki clinched the Constructor and Driver categories.

model_full: Bluebird 4H/T V6 Turbo Maxima Legrand (1986 : PU11)
description: The Bluebird U11 (seventh-generation) was launched in October 1983. The Maxima was launched in October of the following year as the high-end version. As an FF car, it was Japan's first to use the V6 engine. Distinctive was its nose, which was 90mm longer than the U11. The most advanced version, the Legrand, was equipped as standard with a high-quality audio system and an ultrasonic, electronically controlled suspension.

The second-generation Leopard (F31) was launched in February 1986 as a stylish 2-door coupe equipped with a newly developed V6 engine (VG30/VG20). The Altima, the most luxurious grade, featured an electronically controlled suspension with ultrasonic sonar, thereby living up to its concept as a specialty car.

model_full: Nissan EXA Canopy Type B (1986 : KEN13)
description: The third generation Pulsar N13 was released in May 1986 and its coupe model branched off to Nissan EXA (KEN13) in October in the same year. "Coupe" itself was a center of attention because of retractable headlamps and T-Top, but "Canopy" with removable rear roof was a hotter topic as an unconventional unique car. Styling was designed by NDA (former Nissan Design International: NDI) in U.S. Removable rear hatch and canopy could be switched on cars for export, which was unfortunately not allowed in Japan by regulations. T-Top was also removable. So, users could enjoy changing styling. This car is "Type B" of the upper grade with canopy and alloy wheels.

In the 1986 Le Mans, the Nissan (NISMO) team entered a pair of Group C cars. Sadly, the top Japanese machine in the qualifier, the #23 Nissan R86V Nichira (K. Hoshino, K. Matsumoto, A. Suzuki), was forced to retire. However, the #23 Nissan R85V Amada (Masahiro Hasemi, T. Wada, J. Weaver) attracted attention when it came in 16th overall in its debut race.

This is the racing car manufactured for All-Japan Sport Prototype Championship (JSPC) for Group C prototype racing cars in 1986. It has a chassis 86G manufactured by March Engineering Ltd. and a VG30 twin turbo engine of 3-liter V6 that generates over 680ps. It featured the improved aerodymanicperformance by the side radiator system. At 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1986, it finished 24th in the qualifying race with the drivers K. Hoshino, K. Matsumoto and A. Suzuki, but retired in the final. At JSPC, it was driven by K. Hoshino and A. Hagiwara in Round 1 and K. Hoshino and O. Nakakoin Rounds 3 and after. This is colored in the same colors at 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1986.

model_full: Pulsar 3-door Hatchback Milano X-1 Twin-cam (1986 : EN13)
description: The first-generation Pulsar, the N10, was launched in May 1978 and following two full model changes, the N13 was launched on May 7, 1986. The N13’s distinguishing feature was its sporty styling, which combined flowing curved surfaces and sharp lines. Three body types were available: the 3-door hatchback, the 5-door hatchback, and the 4-door saloon. There were also five engines: 4 gasoline (1,300cc, 1,500cc, and 1,600cc twin-cam) and a diesel engine (1,700cc). Altogether, there were 33 basic models in the lineup. The Milano X1 series was a sports-grade model available as a 3-door hatchback or 4-door saloon. The X1 twin-cam was positioned as the sportiest model, at the top end of the series. What attracted attention to this model, together with its newly developed 1,600cc twin-cam engine, was Japan’s first fully automatic full-time 4WD (viscous coupling type), adopted for the 4-door saloon 1500J1. This ground-breaking 4WD system - which automatically ensured optimal torque distribution to the front and rear wheels, providing an easy, safe drive - was highly praised; in fact, it was singled out in the awarding of the 1986-87 Japan Car of the Year title. In January 1987, to commemorate winning the 1986-87 Japan Car of the Year Award, the world’s first triple-viscous, fully automatic full-time 4WD car (Milano X1-E) was launched as a limited-edition model, and available as an option for the Milano X1 twin-cam was Japan’s first viscous LSD.

model_full: Silvia Coupe Twin-cam Turbo RS-X (1986 : S12)
description: The Silvia (CSP311) was introduced in March 1965 and attracted attention as Japan's first specialty car. Following the S10 (launched October 1975) and S110 (launched March 1979), the S12, the fourth-generation model, was launched on August 23, 1983 (its sibling, the Gazelle, was launched at the same time). The Silvia was on the cutting edge, with its innovative styling and lively performance. The S12 was no exception: with its bold front mask and fully retractable headlights, a powerful wedge-type silhouette, and high-performance twin-cam 24-valve FJ20 engine, this unique car was very popular. Two body types were available: a coupe with a notchback roof, and a hatchback with a wide-opening rear gate. Following a minor change in February 1986, the FJ20ET and FJ20E engines were replaced with the new 1.8-liter twin-cam turbo 145PS (net) CA18DET engine, following which all models were powered by the CA18 family. The twin-cam turbo RS-X was the top-of-the-line model for both the coupe and hatchback series. Following a minor change in February 1986, it was equipped with an electronically controlled 4-speed lockup automatic transmission with overdrive that automatically switches between power and economy modes.

model_full: Skyline 4-door Hardtop GTS Twin-cam 24V Turbo (1986 : KRR31)
description: The seventh-generation Skyline (R31) was launched on August 19, 1985 at a time when peoples' lifestyles and values were changing greatly. The R31 was a high-profile model that aimed to offer the sort of cutting-edge design and performance sought by a mature automotive society. The public already liked the R31's refined styling, which hinted at its superior drivability, but when a stylish 4-door hardtop was introduced, the Skyline's popularity soared even higher. A high-quality driving experience was the goal, and this was realized by the powerful, newly developed 6-cylinder in-line twin-cam 24-valve turbocharged RB20DET engine. These twin-cam engine models were also equipped with such advanced technologies as the breakthrough HICAS (High Capacity Actively-controlled Suspension) rear-wheel steering system. HICAS turns the rear wheels by as much as 0.5 of a degree in response to steering angle and car speed. A total of 32 basic models were available within the 2 types of body- 4-door sedan and 4-door hardtop - as well as 6 engines (RB20DET, RB20DE, RB20ET, RB20E, CA18S, and RD28). Starting with a 2-door sports coupe (equipped with a ceramic turbo engine) launched on May 22, 1986, "GTS" was positioned as a the twin-cam grade (later a twin-cam 4-door hardtop was also introduced), featuring HICAS, 4-wheel disc brakes, high-support seats and full-wheel covers as standard equipment.

“Be-1” was exhibited as reference at the 26th Tokyo Motor Show in 1985. Its concept was “Coziness-oriented Car.” The car body was based on the first generation March K10, but its styling and interior reminded people of good old cars. The name come from “Plan B-1”. When the model was rolled out with a production limit of 10,000 in January 1987, more than 10,000 orders were made, and buyers were decided by lottery. Be-1 triggered the production of Nissan Pike Car Series of PAO and FIGARO. The meaning of the word “pike” was “edgy”, and pike cars were highly unique cars that were manufactured in limited volume.

This custom-made open car, based on the Be-1, was designed as a relief car for use at the Yokohama Stadium, the home ground of the Yokohama BayStars baseball team. The passenger seat is slightly raised. After debuting in 1987, it was used for about 2 years. A famous pitcher, Kazuhiro "Daimajin" Sasaki, who used to play in Seattle Mariners, used this car when he was in Yokohama BayStars before he became a major leaguer.

model: Cedric 4-door H/T V20 Turbo Urban G
model_full: Cedric 4-door H/T V20 Turbo Urban G (1987 : Y30)
description: The sixth-generation (Y30) was launched in June 1983. This model was available in three series: the 4-door sedan, the 4-door hardtop, and the estate wagon. The main engine was a newly developed V6 (VG30/20). In January 1987, to commemorate the production of 1 million VG engines, the Urban G - a special limited edition (500 cars) based on the Urban - was launched.

"Be-1" was exhibited as reference at the 26th Tokyo Motor Show in 1985. Its concept was "Coziness-oriented Car". The car body was based on the first generation March K10, but its styling and interior reminded people of good old cars. The name come from "Plan B-1". When the model was rolled out with a production limit of 10,000 in January 1987, more than 10,000 orders were made and buyers were decided by lottery. Be-1 triggered the production of Nissan Pike Car Series of PAO and FIGARO. The meaning of the word "pike" was "edgy", and pike cars were highly unique cars that were manufactured by limited small volume.

MID4 is an experimental car to exhibit the achievements of R&D at motor shows. The model name comes from a supercar with a midshipengine layout and a four-wheel drive system. This car “MID4 II” was exhibited at the 27th Tokyo Motor Show in 1987. Mounted engine, “VG30DETT”, 3-liter V6 DOHC twin-turbo with intercooler, generated 330ps. The suspension type was Double Wishbone for front and Multilink for rear with steering system named “HICAS”. Although this model was never sold in the market, many of its new technologies were applied to the Nissan 300ZX (Z32) rolled out in 1989 and the Skyline GT-R (R32).

The first-generation March (K10) debuted at the 1981 Tokyo Motor Show. Its name was chosen from among thousands of entries submitted by the general public, and it was launched in October 1982. This particular vehicle was a rental machine built by NISMO for the "March Little Dynamite Cup Race", an event first held in 1987. The engine is fitted with both a turbo and supercharger. A super-turbo version with the same specifications was launched in January 1989.

model: Skyline 2-door Sports Coupe GTS-X Twin-cam 24V Turbo
model_full: Skyline 2-door Sports Coupe GTS-X Twin-cam 24V Turbo (1987: HR31)
description: The seventh generation Skyline R31 was rolled out with the copy "This is urban engineering" in 1985. It adopted various innovations such as "RB" engine (6-cyl., DOHC), ceramic turbo charger, and "HICAS" four-wheel drive system, but was talked critically that significantly enlarged body, elimination of 2-door model from lineup, and luxury-car line advocating "driver-friendly high performance" didn't fit Skyline. The long-awaited 2-door coupe was added in 1986. "GTS-R" won the title at Japan Touringcar Championship (JTC) in 1989, publicizing its existence. This is "GTS-X" with the engine of 6-cyl. 4-valve DOHC with turbo, 180ps mounted on 2-door coupe and special aluminum wheels.

The seventh-generation Skyline (R31) was launched in August 1985 and this model is well remembered as being the first to reintroduce the 6-cylinder DOHC engine (discontinued with the C110). In May 1986, the coupe GTS appeared, and in August 1987, after a minor change, the coupe GTS-R (RB20DET-R: 210PS engine) - based on Group A race specifications - was sold as a limited edition (800 units).

model_full: Cedric Cima Type II Limited (1988 : FY31)
description: Following its debut at the 27th Tokyo Motor Show in 1987, the FY31 (first-generation Cima) was officially launched in January 1988 as Japan's first car to sport a V6 twin-cam turbo engine. Without the constraints of a compact car frame, its generous styling and comfortable interior made it stand apart. The top-of-the-line Type II Limited model was also equipped with an electronically controlled air suspension.

A new model was rolled out in 1988 without the name being publicized in advance. The target was people of early 30s. It was "Cefiro" sedan, the third model of large-sized sedan following Skyline and Laurel. It featured "Cefiro combination", i.e. there were 3 types of 2000cc engine, 3 kinds of suspension, 9 body colors, 3 interior materials and 2 interior colors, and a customer could choose any of them for his/her own car. That is why early models have no names to indicate their grade and many "Recommended Combinations" were shown in catalogs. Many advanced technologies were adopted such as multilink rear suspension and HICAS-II. This is the model of early days in bluish silver.

The R88C was powered by the VRH30, newly developed for the 24 Hours of Le Mans race. The car too had evolved considerably, featuring a longer wheelbase to improve driving ease and Nissan's original cowl design. It came in 15th overall in the 24 Hours of Le Mans race in 1988, and it best result in the All Japan Sports Prototype Championship (JSPC) was 3rd position.

A distinguishing feature of the R88C was that it was powered by a new engine, the VRH30, developed for racing at Le Mans. Driven by #24 YHP's No.1 driver, Masahiro Hasemi, it took part in the 1988 and 1989 JSPC races (up to the 2nd round in 1989). In the 1988 season, it came in 3rd in the 1st round (Fuji) and 5th round (Suzuka). In 1989, it was 3rd in the 2nd round (Fuji) and 4th in the World Sports Prototype Championship (WSPC) 1st round (Suzuka).

The fifth generation Silvia (S13), rolled out in May 1988 in Japan with the tagline “Art Force Silvia,” was a beautifully shaped coupe and became very popular especially among young people. It received the Good Design Award selected by Ministry of International Trade and Industry and Car of The Year Japan as a proof of its beauty and popularity. FR (front engine and rear drive) drive system also attracted drivers. The engine mounted on the original model was 1.8-liter “CA18” DOHC. An NA (natural aspiration) of 135ps was mounted for “J’s” and “Q’s”, and a turbo-charged version of 175ps for “K’s”. In 1991, all the engines were changed to 2-liter “SR20” DOHC to enhance the power. NISSAN 180SX that shared the platform with the Silvia was rolled out in 1989 and also became a big hit. This car is “Q’s” equipped with CA18DE engine.

The sixth-generation Sunny B12 Series released in 1985 was a hit model given the nickname "Trad Sunny" from the advertising copy "TRAD SUNNY" that appealed to universal values regardless of the era. The youthful, clean styling, high-quality image evoked by the word "trad", together with the appealing TV commercial featuring several hit songs by the late-era Beatles contributed to the rejuvenation of the aging Sunny owner demographic. The body types lined up with the 3-door hatchback and 5-door "California" in addition to the 4-door sedan, while the 3-door vehicle had a unique grade composition with grade names of "303", "305", and "306" depending on the engine size. In 1986 the variation was broadened with the addition of the sharp 3-door coupe "RZ-1". The car here is the medium class 1500 EX Saloon that had undergone minor change in 1987.

This Silvia (export name: Nissan 200SX) was driven by Mike Kirkland in the 36th Safari Rally of 1988; it came 2nd overall and also won the A4 class (over 2,000cc, 2WD). That year's Safari Rally was very hazardous due to heavy rain preceding the event and only 14 cars completed the course, but the March won in the A3 class (1,600cc-2,000cc), making Nissan a 2-class champion.

The 7th generation Skyline R31 was rolled out in 1985. It was in 1986, the next year, that the longed-for 2-door coupe series was added to the line. The limited edition "GTS-R" coupe with the engine output of 210ps was rolled out in 1987 as base model for Group A touring cars. This is the car manufactured by NME (Nissan Motorsports Europe; the activity base of NISMO in Europe). It participated in European Touring Car Championship (ETC) races in 1988 with the drivers A. Grice and W. Percy. It finished 6th in the overall category at Total 24 Hours of Spa Francorchamps, one of the Triple Crown of endurance races, driven by A. Grice, W. Percy and A. Olofsson.

The fourth-generation model (Z32) was launched in July 1989. The only available engine was a 3-liter V6, but it came with or without a turbo. There were 2 types of body available: the two-seater and 2/2. The vehicle shown was used as a pace car for races held on the Fuji Speedway. Its suspension was strengthened for driving on the circuit.

The fourth generation Fairlady Z (Z32), also known as 300ZX, was released in '89. One of the features was the styling into which innovations and Z's traditions were integrated; wide and low styling, heavily slanted headlamps, cabin-forward form and short overhang. There were two models in early days; the traditional 2-seater and the "2by2" for 4 passengers. Mounted engine was VG30DE of 3000cc, V6 4-valve DOHC with the choice of twin turbo or natural aspiration. Nissan's latest chassis technologies of the time such as 4-wheel multilink suspensions, super HICAS, and aluminum caliper and opposing 4-piston brakes were implemented. This car is the top grade "2by2" model, Fairlady 300ZX twin turbo.

March (Micra in overseas countries) has been Nissan's No.1 compact car since it was rolled out in 1982. The first generation was exhibited as a concept car "NX-018" at Tokyo Motor Show in 1981 and, after a major advertising campaign for the name, rolled out in October 1982. Economically efficient and user-friendly basic performance and plain but fashionable styling attracted mainly active women. Collet, with fancier interior such as plaid textile for seats and vanity mirrors attached to sun visors on driver's and passenger's seats, became popular among a wide range of drivers. This car is Collet in 1989 with optional canvas top.

Following the Be-1, the PAO rolled out as the second model of “Pike Car” series. Pike car is a generic name of playful yet “edgy” cars manufactured on the condition of limited volume production. PAO was exhibited as a concept car at the 27th Tokyo Motor Show in 1987 and was rolled out in January 1989. Total production exceeded 30 thousand units. Its interior and exterior were designed in a retrospective style under the concept of “adventurous spirit” which became a big hit. The name PAO comes from the Chinese word meaning a Mongolian portable dwelling. This car is equipped with a canvas top.

The first-generation Prairie released in 1982 was the pioneering "world's first minivan" - an unprecedented, futuristic sedan/multi-use sedan. The following, second-generation model debuted in September 1988 to combine aerodynamic, curved styling and higher driving performance with the concept of "a car offering relaxation and fun to people who cherish activities with the family". The styling underwent a drastic turnaround to a one motion style with the low nose leading gently to the long cabin, from the two-box form of the first generation model. Although the first-generation's central pillarless structure was discontinued, the convenient slide doors on both sides which were unusual at the time were continued. The car here is the J7 ATTESA, an early, top-grade 7-seater and which was equipped with the new-generation full-time 4WD system which was being deployed on a large scale by Nissan at the time, starting with the Bluebird.

In 1989 Group C cars evolved into the monster machine "Nissan R89C" with the max. power of more than 800ps by switching the chassis manufacturer from March Engineering Ltd. to Lola Cars International Ltd. and changing 3-liter engine to 3.5-liter VRH35 (V8 DOHC). Its main features are more sleek-looking exterior and a fullscaleimplementation of the telemetry device. In JSPC, it made a debut at Round 3:Fuji GT 500mile Race. At Round 5:Fuji GT 1000km Race, Car No.24 YHP (the drivers Masahiro Hasemiand A. Olofsson) finished 8th and showed a glimpesof its potential. This is the genuine machine of No.23 Calsonic Nissan R89C steered by Kazuyoshi Hoshino and Toshio Suzuki.

The eighth generation Skyline R32 was rolled out in May 1989. Three months later, the “GT-R” was brought back after the 16-year absence. The engine was a specially designed “RB26DETT” of 2.6-liter inline 6-cylinder DOHC twin turbo and generated maximum power of 280ps. The drive system was called “ATTESA E-TS” that was the electronically controlled torque split 4WD which transmitted the best torque to all the wheels. It even had the 4-wheel multilink suspension. These equipment realized one of the best performances all over the world as a sedan-based sport car. This GT-R has a record of amazing 29 victories and no defeat for 4 seasons at Japan Touring Car Championship from 1990 through 1993. It also received a high reputation at overseas races like Spa-Francorchamps24 Hours.

The fifth-generation Silvia (S13) - descended from the first-generation CSP311, launched in March 1965 - was introduced on May 17, 1988. This car was developed as a compact specialty coupe with an emphasis on beauty and the driving experience. Exterior and interior shared the same design theme, and numerous advanced technologies, such as the multilink rear suspension, were incorporated to enhance performance. For this reason, the car was greatly appreciated by the younger generation, who are very particular about the way a car handles. The S13 was regarded as a high-quality product, and in 1988 it received the Good Design Award by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry. The natural lines and curved surfaces of the streamlined styling set the S13 apart. Together with its interior - which, from dashboard to door trim and center console, featured a unified design - this car had the unmistakable look of a specialty coupe. The multilink rear suspension was a new idea that was later adopted for the Skyline. Together with the HICAS-II 4-wheel steering system (option) and the 1.8-liter twin-cam engine (CA18DE/CA18DET), the car was equipped to provide an excellent drive. The S13 was available in 3 grades*: K's, Q's, and J's. The top-of-the-line K's was equipped with the S-pack (rear spoiler, projected headlights, 195/60R15 tires, etc.) which accentuated the sporty character of the car. Following a minor change in January 1991, the engine was changed to the twin-cam SR20DE/SR20DET. *The names of the three models were derived from the three court cards: King (K), Queen (Q), and Jack (J).

model_full: Nissan Sunny RZ-1 Twincam NISMO (1989: EB12)
description: The sixth generation Sunny B12 was rolled out in 1985. The original lineup was 4-door sedan that became a big hit, and crisp 3-door hatchback. The lineup was expanded in 1986 by adding "RZ-1", 3-door hatchback coupe of edgy form, and "California", utility 5-door hatchback. A high-performance version "Twin-cam series" with 4-valve DOHC engine was also added in that year. This is "RZ-1 Twin-cam NISMO" of special spec based on a twin-cam model of RZ-1, bearing the name of "Nissan Motorsports International (NISMO)" established In 1984. It was a "hot" car with special suspension, special aerodynamic exterior parts, special leather-wrapped steering wheel, and white instrument panel.

The S-Cargo rolled out together with PAO in January 1989, got very popular for its snail-like styling. The name “S-Cargo” is coined by combining the French word “escargot” that means snail with a “cargo”. The luggage room was 1,230mm high and very useful, and the body sides were often used as advertising billboard. The instrument panel was very unique; a table-like instrument panel with the big speedometer located in the center and the shift lever below the speedometer. The S-Cargo is the only commercial vehicle in the “Pike Car” series and is still very popular.

The eighth generation Bluebird U12 was released in 1987 with "ATTESA", the groundbreaking fulltime 4WD system that used viscous coupling in center differential. "CA" engine series on U12 was replaced with "SR" engine series at a minor change in 1989. U12 was one of the sportiest models among generations of Skyline and was equipped with a lot of new technologies. It even had a variation of rally car "SSS-R" based on "SSS ATTESA Limited" of full-time 4WD with turbo engine. "SSS-R" won the championship of Japan Rally Championship in 1988. This car is "SSS ATTESA X" of 4WD with SR20DE engine of 140ps, STC (Super Toe Control) and viscous LSD (limited slip differential).
