The first generation Cima FPY31 was exhibited at the 27th Tokyo Motor Show in 1987 and rolled out in January 1988. The Cima was designed uniquely for large sedan segment only, and made waves across Japan due to sleek body line, spacious room, high performance of Japan's first turbocharged V6 DOHC engine, and electronically controlled air suspension. The sales increased after the commodity tax was abolished in 1989 and affordability increased, which triggered the so-called "large car boom" in Japan. This car is "Type II Limited," the top grade of this line with a 3.0-liter turbocharged V6 DOHC engine (VG30DET) that generated 255ps.

The first-generation Laurel, the C30, was launched as Japan's first 1,800cc car in April 1968. The Laurel achieved its status as a pure "owner's car", a personal passenger car that was not to be made available in taxi or van versions. The C33 (sixth-generation) Laurel, which was launched on the December 16, 1988, was designed as a high-quality 4-door salon that would appeal to a mature taste. Its distinctive styling combined strong flat surfaces with generous curves in a mature form, while a bold-looking front-mask and character lines running down the sides created an impression of refinement. With ingenious use of curved surfaces and high-quality materials, the designers created an even more pleasing cabin interior. A choice of 6-cylinder in-line engines was available. Nissan's own advanced technologies were used to good effect, as demonstrated by the DUET-EA (engine-transmission integrated control) system to ensure smooth acceleration, the multi-link rear suspension to provide both improved control and greater ride comfort, and the HICAS-II, a 4-wheel steering system for greater driving versatility. Also, the new "Club L" and the "Club S" versions of the top-of-the-line Medalist model were equipped with an 8-way driver's power seat, genuine leather seats, leather-wrapped steering wheel, and genuine wood-grained instrument cluster as standard.

The Maxima started out as a top-of-the-line Bluebird. The PU11 (first-generation model) was launched on October 17, 1984. With the first model change (J30) on October 21, 1988, however, it was recognized as an independent series. The J30 only came as a 4-door sedan. The model powered by the VG30E V6 engine featured an electronic 4-speed automatic transmission with DUET-EA integrated control, as well as the DUET-SS "supersonic" suspension. Safety was enhanced, with those models equipped with ventilated front disc brakes having ABS as standard. At the time of the launch, there were only two models on offer: Type I (standard: 4-wheel disc brakes, ABS, fully automatic air conditioner, aluminum wheels), and Type II (Type I plus DUET-EA, Bose sound system, ASCD as standard). However, on August 24 1989 the sporty SE was added, followed by the luxury 300SV on January 24, 1991. The SE, which went on sale in August 1989, featured the DUET-EA system, 2-stage shock absorbers, and electronically controlled power assisted steering. Its standard equipment included a "blackout" exterior (black trim moldings and rear finisher), a rear spoiler, leather-wrapped 4-spoke steering wheel, ASCD, Bose sound system, and fully automatic air conditioner.

180SX was a hatchback coupe that shared the platform with Silvia S13. 240SX/200SX were released in North America and Europe as 1989 year model prior to the release in Japan in 1989. It realized the aerodynamic performance of Cd 0.3 due to the flowing body with retractable headlamps. It had CA18DET engine of 1800cc, 4-valve DOHC with turbo for "Silvia K's," multilink rear suspension and HICAS-II, which enabled handling stability, traveling performance and comfortability to be balanced in a high level. This car is "TYPE II" of the early model. 180SX continued without any change of basic design until 1998 and had a significant influence on younger people at the time.

The first-generation March released in 1982 was a compact car based on an original styling layout draft by Italdesign led by Giorgetto Giugiaro from Italy, the maestro of car design. The lifespan of the product was unusually long at around 10 years, and additional releases were made from time to time, like the Canvas Top, the Turbo, and the 5-door car. The Super Turbo here is the road car version of the March R rally car and in consideration of participation in competition, its displacement has been daringly shrunk to 930cc from a normal 987cc to keep it in the 1.6l class even if a turbo coefficient of 1.4 is applied. Also, it is equipped with a supercharger and a turbocharger with differing characteristics, and is set up to achieve high output from low to high revolution. This March Super Turbo was the only commercially available car in Japan to have this kind of twin charging engine.

The R90C was developed jointly with the Lola Cars International company, but the R91C was 100% manufactured by Nissan. The "CP" refers to JSPC specifications, while "CK" means WSPC specifications; a difference can be seen in the shape of the rear spoiler. The yellow No.27 car is an R90CK from the UK (NME)*. Following Nissan's decision to pull out of world championship racing, this machine (Nakatani, Volker Weidler) took part in the JSPC as the "From-A R91CK Nissan". *NME: Nissan Motorsports Europe

There were 2 types of R90 - the R90C made at Oppama, and the R90CK made by NME (NISMO Europe) - differing in cowl and rear spoiler design. The R90CK was entered in WSPC including Le Mans, in 1990 and 1991; it also took part in US endurance races. The machine shown was entered by the US-based NPTI* Team in the 1991 Daytona 24 Hours. *NPTI: Nissan Performance Technology Incorporated

A total of five R90CP/CK cars took part in the 1990 Le Mans race, entered by teams from Japan, the US, and Britain. The NPTI team, which contested the US IMSA Series, ran a pair of R90CKs. When the results were in, No.83 had come in 4th in the qualifier but retired in the final race, while No.84 (B. Earl, M. Roe, S. Millen) was 25th in the qualifier and 17th in the main event.

Developed jointly with the Lola Cars International company, the R90C car was the fruit of global strategic planning. It incorporated significant advances, such as a newly designed monocoque body offering greater rigidity. The R90CK made by NME took part in international endurance championships, such as Le Mans, and also the IMSA series in USA. This machine was entered by the US-based NPTI Team in the 1992 Daytona 24 Hours (GTP class).

The Group C races, which started in 1983, evolved into the All Japan Championships from 1990. Nissan chalked up three consecutive wins in this series, and the first of those was achieved by this machine (Masahiro Hasemi and A. Olofsson). The chassis of the R90C was a British Lola, but about 70% of the parts were made by Nissan and NISMO.

This is Nissan R90CP YHP (driven by M. Hasemi and A. Olofsson) for All-Japan Sports Prototype Championship (JSPC) in 1991. The car number "1" is the proof of the champion of the previous year. It ran the season-opening race only. R91CP ran the 2nd race and after. R90CP was Nissan's original racing car for JSPC and Le Mans in 1990. While R90CK (used by NME and NPTI) adopted revised Lola chassis, R90CP adopted chassis thoroughly revised by Nissan and original cowl designed by Yoshitaka Suzuka. R91CP was 100% Nissan-made with Nissan's original full carbon monocoque. R90CP, R91CP and R92CP won Drivers Title and Manufacturers Title in 3 successive years from 1990 through 92.

The President was Japan's first authentic full-size car. The first-generation model (150) debuted on October 21, 1965. This was followed by a full model change (250) in August 1973, and the third-generation JHG50 was announced on October 24, 1990. The styling of the JHG50, representing the first full model change in 17 years, was distinguished by the elegant vertical design of its front grille and the grand proportions resulting from its long wheelbase. The interior was enhanced by the extended wheelbase (+180mm) and reduced noise (62dB in the cabin at 100km/h), while comfort was improved further with silk wool seats (standard), Connolly leather seats (option), power seats with auto-lifter, and a central control for the rear seats. Powered by the VH45DE engine (V8 4.5-liter DOHC), offering a maximum output of 270PS, the JHG50 featured the very latest of Nissan's technologies, as demonstrated by its 4-wheel multilink hydraulic active suspension, V-TCS traction control with viscous LSD, and engine automatic integrated control. With a minor change in February 1992, the short-wheelbase JS Series was added to the lineup, and in April 1993 a model was launched with the world's first rear-seat SRS airbags .

The N13, launched in May 1986, received high praise for its newly developed twin-cam engine. As Japan's first full-time 4WD, it was awarded the 1986-87 Car of the Year Japan. Both 4-door saloon and hatchback models were available. The "Trenda" was launched in January 1990 as a "good value" series (equipped with air conditioner and stereo as standard).

The GT-R, reintroduced with the R32 (launched August 1989), made its debut at the opening race of the All Japan Championship in March 1990. In the 4 seasons running up to the last All Japan Championship, held in1993, the GT-R achieved a spectacular record, winning all 29 rounds. This No. 12 Calsonic ("CalsonicKansei" at present) Skyline (K. Hoshino/Masahiko Kageyama) was victorious in 1990 and 1993.

The eighth generation Skyline R32 was rolled out in May 1989, which became a hottest topic as the revival of "GT-R" after 16 years of discontinuation. R32 was entirely renovated from form to suspension. Sizes were reduced for high dynamic performance, which was taken favorably as "return to Skyline as it should be" by many fans. The lineup was pillared hardtop 4-door sedan and 2-door coupe. This is" GTS-t TypeM", the hottest model as of May 1989. High cornering performance and stability achieved by 4-wheel multilink suspension was talked about a lot. "TypeM" was very popular as handy roadworthy GT-car while "GT-R" was born for touring car races and not everyone could drive it.

NX Coupe (100NX for export), a coupe model of the seventh generation Sunny B13, was rolled out in 1990. It was a cute and casual coupe, unusual for Sunny, while the previous model "RZ-1" had an edgy look. Its curvy form was designed for female users in North America by NDI*. Motifs of North America's favorite 300ZX (Z32) appeared throughout the car and there was T-Top as option. Engine variations were 1500cc, 1600cc, and 1800cc of 4-valve DOHC. The copy "Wow! A time machine?" and TV commercial were novel. Especially commercial CG in which personified NX coupe morphed became a hot topic. This is NX Coupe Type B in "Yellow Pearl". *NDI: Nissan Design International Inc., current Nissan Design America, Inc.

Cars for both city and off-road driving were simultaneously born in mid 1980s when people started driving pickup trucks and 4WD cars to go for recreation. NISSAN Terrano rolled out in 1986 was one of the cutting-edge SUVs. Although the base was Nissan Pickup D21, it was totally different from traditional 4WD cars. Suspensions were double wishbone for front and 5-link for rear to achieve traveling performance on rough road and comfort on pavement. And it had a form of urban taste designed by NDI (Nissan Design International) in North America. It is still popular in North America market as "Pathfinder". This car is "V6-3000 R3M" with 2-door body and powerful VG30E engine.

The Figaro FK10 was a "2-door coupe just for yourself" that was exhibited at 1989 Tokyo Motor Show and received favorable reviews. It was rolled out in 1991 with the limited volume of 20,000 units. The Figaro was the fourth "Pike car" following the Be-1, PAO and S-Cargo. Its concept was "Tokyo Nouvelle Vague" and a trilogy short film "FIGARO STORY" in line with the concept was created featuring this model -quite unusual marketing activities were implemented. The Figaro had an elegant styling with unique open top, white leather interior trims, specially-designed instruments including meters and audio panels.any of them were carefully finished. 4 body colors were available -"Emerald"," Paleaqua"," Lapisgray (grayish purple)", and "Topazmist(muddy yellow)". This car is in Emerald.

Infiniti Q45 was rolled out in November 1989 as the flagship model of the new premium brand "INFINITI" in the U.S. market. The Q45 went on sale in Japan as well. With the concept "Japan Original", Nissan pursued the concept of values unique to Japan but acknowledged also in foreign countries, which resulted in a unique styling without front grille and adoption of Japanese traditional craftworks such as cloisonné front emblem. Mounted was a newly developed 4.5-liter V8 DOHC engine, and the world's first "Hydraulic Active Suspension" was equipped in the "Selection Package". This car is equipped with red leather seats and the standard suspension system in Burgundy (PM) body.

model: Nissan Cedric Twincam Turbo Gran Turismo SV
model_full: Nissan Cedric Twincam Turbo Gran Turismo SV (1991: Y31)
description: The seventh generation Cedric/the eighth generation Gloria Y31 rolled out in 1987 was the first model designed to realize "the fun of driving" for high-end passenger cars. The concept was embodied in "Gran Turismo" series newly set out besides "Brougham". The high-end car market marveled at traveling performance improved by excellent hardware such as Cedric's/Gloria's first 4-wheel independent suspension and "VG20DET" engine (2000cc, V6, 4-valve DOHC with turbo). VG20DET was the power unit of high performance in which low-friction ceramic turbo was adopted and first equipped on this car, Y31 Gran Turismo. The horsepower was 185ps in early days and 210ps after 1989.

engine: Ni-Cd Battery + Quadrupolar AC induction motor x 2
description: Nissan is a company that has researched electric vehicle (EV) over many decades. Nissan FEV is the experimental high-performance EV exhibited at the 29th Tokyo Motor Show in 1991. Nissan achieved a high-performance car that lived up to the concept of "a compact car that is people-friendly and environmentally friendly"; that employed a "super fast electric charging system" that could charge to 40% in only six minutes, even though research had not started on the automotive lithium-ion battery that is now the global standard in current EVs; extremely aerodynamic styling with a Cd (coefficient drag) of 0.19; independent control of left and right front wheels and low-rolling, low-resistance tires achieved with two compact, lightweight, high-output, high-efficiency AC induction motors; and, achieved a cruising distance of 250 km on one charge, acceleration from 0 to 400 m in 20 seconds, and a top speed of 130 km/h. The car here is a vehicle that was kept in Nissan Research Center. Nissan's Prototype Division restored the interior and exterior in 2025.

The Figaro FK10 was a "2-door coupe just for yourself" that was exhibited at 1989 Tokyo Motor Show and received favorable reviews. It was rolled out in 1991 with the limited volume of 20,000 units. The Figaro was the fourth "Pike car" following the "Be-1", "PAO" and S-Cargo. Its concept was "Tokyo Nouvelle Vague" and a trilogy short film "FIGARO STORY" in line with the concept was created featuring this model - quite unusual marketing activities were implemented. The Figaro had an elegant styling with unique open top, white leather interior trims, specially-designed instruments including meters and audio panels... any of them were carefully finished. 4 body colors were available "Emerald", "Pale aqua", "Lapis gray (grayish purple)", and "Topaz mist (muddy yellow)". This car is in Pale aqua.

model_full: Nissan Patrol (Safari) Std. Roof Granroad (1991: VRGY60)
description: "Nissan Patrol" born in 1951 was the Nissan's first 4WD car and has been favored all over the world due to its rigidity and high traveling performance. 6 generations of Patrol models were rolled out in 70 years from 1951 to 2021. It was known as "Safari" from 1980 to the 2000s in Japan. Y60 rolled out in 1987 is known as the second generation "Safari" in Japan and as the fourth generation "Patrol" in overseas markets. It was the model that placed emphasis on leisure use of 4WD cars as the copy "King of Adventure" represented. Features included the magnificent form with blister fenders and the comfortable ride with the traditional traveling performance.

This silver No.61 car was driven by Hideki Okada and T. Danielsson of Team Take One. Badged as "Kokuyo, Take One, Nissan", it raced alongside other Group C cars in the All Japan Championship of 1992, the final year it was held. In the Fuji 1000km race, the car's second race since its debut, it succeeded in coming in 2nd. This machine was fitted with Dunlop tires because of sponsorship requirements.

The history of Group C racing cars of Nissan started in 1983. At first, Nissan engines were mounted on chassis manufactured by March Engineering Ltd. or Lola Cars International Ltd. to run at WEC (World Endurance Championship) races and domestic endurance races (JSPC). But the number of in-house products drastically increased on and after Nissan R90. This is R91CP with new carbon monocoquedesigned by Nissan. This is the memorable machine that achieved the first overall victory as Japanese car at Rolex 24 At Daytona in 1992, steered by M. Hasemi, K. Hoshino and T. Suzuki. The excellent total balance of powerful VRH35Z engine and carefully tuned chassis led to this feat.

This open car used to be lent out by Nissan for use in special events, such as transporting sumo champions in victory parades, or as the leading car in a marathon. Because of the special situations in which it was to be used, it was designed as an electric car to lighten the burden on the environment. Its top speed is 40km/h and maximum driving distance on one full charge is 100km. Its acceleration is impressive, doing 0-30km/h in 3 seconds, and 0-40km/h in 9.5 seconds.

The fourth-generation Pulsar, the N14, was launched in August 1990. Using the same SR20DET twin-cam turbo engine (230PS) as the Bluebird SSS-R, the GTI-R debuted in the World Rally Championship at the 1991 Safari Rally and performed well in other WRC events over the next two years. This commemorative car was driven by D. Llewellin's team in the 1991 Acropolis Rally.

After appearing at the 1987 Tokyo Motor Show, the Saurus was further enhanced for its racing debut. This car, called "Saurus Jr.", was its derivative model debuted in 1991 Tokyo Auto Salon. Around 120 units were produced and it was also served as a school car at the Nissan Racing School, helping to foster aspiring professional racing car drivers. The engine is MA10E, a popular Nissan engine found on the March.

After 16 years, the "GT-R" name was reintroduced with the eighth-generation R32. The combination of the RB26DETT engine (maximum output: 280PS) and ATTESA E-TS proved too much for its rivals at the All Japan Touring Car Championships (Group A). This vehicle won the 1993 Tsukuba 12h Endurance Race and was entered in the 1994 Daytona 24 Hours (N1 specifications). *Note: The R32GT-R was launched in August 1989.

RB26DETT engine and electronically controlled torque split 4WD "ATTESA E-TS" made Skyline GT-R R32 one of the most popular models in the line. It won all of 29 Group A touring car races in Japan and took the pole position at every race, which made a significant mark in the motorsport history in Japan. It ran at Total 24 Hours at Spa-Francorchamps, one of the Triple Crown of endurance races, from 1990 to 1992. No. 25, steered by N. Hattori, A. Olofsson and D. Brabham, won the championship in the overall category with the record of the highest speed/longest distance in 1991. R32 also finished 6th in overall category of Group N with the drivers T. Kinoshita, K. O'dorand D. Schoysman.
NA

The third generation Leopard JPY32 released in 1992 was renamed to Leopard J. Ferie and upgraded to a high-end sedan based on Cedric/Gloria Y32. "J. Ferie" was a coined word for the French word "jour ferie (holiday)". It was released as "Infiniti J30" in North America at the same time. It was an unconventional high-end car with curvy styling with downwardly inclining tail that was contentious in Japan, and interior and design similar to those of British high-end cars. A driver also could enjoy driving a powerful car with high performance achieved by two types of engines; 8-cyl. V-type 4130cc and 6-cyl. V-type 2960cc. This car is "Type L" with the 3-liter engine.

The fourth generation Fairlady Z (Z32) was released in 1989, twenty years after the release of the first generation. The styling with refined beauty and sharpness of Z such as curvy wide & low proportion, extremely slanted headlamps and short overhang representing high dynamic performance became a popular topic. The lineup included two bodies; 2-seater and 2+2, and two types of VG30 engine of V6, 4-valve DOHC and 3000cc; twin turbo and natural aspiration. Features included the leading-edge chassis technologies such as 4-wheel multi-link suspension, super HICAS and aluminum caliper opposed 4-pison brakes. This car is U.S. spec "Nissan 300ZX" manufactured in 1992, with naturally aspirated VG30DE engine.

The fourth-generation (Z32) was launched exactly 20 years after the first-generation Fairlady Z in July 1989. The convertible was officially released in August 1992, after its exhibition at the 1991 Tokyo Motor Show. The car is based on the two-seater 300ZX and features an independent trunk lid. The engine was a non-turbo VG30DE (230PS).

With a change in vehicle regulations, turbochargers were banned from Group C cars from 1993 onwards. In response, Nissan developed a naturally aspirated 3.5-liter engine, mounting it in the NP35 (JSPC specifications) and P35 (US IMSA specifications). However, with the cancellation of the World Championship, Nissan suspended its racing activities and this NP35 only made one appearance in the All Japan Championship.

Pulsar GTI-R was developed as top performance model of the fourth generation Pulsar N14 to compete in World Rally Championship (WRC) under "Group A" regulations and was rolled out in 1990. Mechanisms featured 2000cc turbo engine that generated 230ps and 4WD controlled by "ATTESA". It is very popular as a road car of impressive appearance with a giant hood bulge that houses a large intercooler and a giant rear spoiler. It started to participate in WRC in 1991. The best result was the third place at Swedish Rally in 1992, but Nissan decided to withdraw from WRC in the same year. It was for only 2 years that the machine joined WRC. However, it won the title of the year in Group N and proved its high potential.

NISSAN challenged grueling overseas rallies for several decades with varieties of machines such as the first rally car DATSUN Sedan, Bluebird, 240Z, Violet and Silvia. "GTI-R" that is the sports model of the 4th generation Pulsar (Model N14) rolled out in 1990 also participated in World Rally Championship (WRC) under the Group A regulations in 1991 and 1992. The reason Pulsar was chosen was that a high-performance DOHC turbo engine and the 4WD system called "ATTESA" (Advanced Total Traction Engineering System for All) could be packed in a compact body. The engine output of the works machines reached 300ps. This is the genuine machine that S. Blomqvistand B. Melanderdrove at Lombard RAC Rally of Great Britain in 1992.

The R92CP is a model for the history books, having won the JSPC for three years running (Constructor's and Driver's Championships 1990-92). Its specifications are basically the same as the R91CP; "R92CP" was just the entry name. #24 YHP's results in the 6 races of the '92 season were 1st, 4th, 5th, 4th, 4th, and 4th. Masahiro Hasemi came in 5th in the Driver's Championship, with J. Krosnoff following in 9th position.

In the 1991 season, K. Hoshino and Toshio Suzuki (Calsonic) easily won the Driver's Championship with 5 wins in 7 races. In 1992, the same team notched up 5 wins in 6 races (the other going to YHP) in a splendid defense of their throne. This is what led to Nissan taking the double title - Constructor's and Driver's Championships - for three years in a row, a glorious achievement.

In 1989, after a gap of 16 years, the "GT-R" name was reintroduced with the eighth-generation Skyline, and it returned to racing in 1990. This vehicle was the ZEXEL Racing Team's group N specification (N1) GT-R. It was entered in the N1 Endurance Round Series (Japan) and the Spa-Francorchamps 24 Hours (Belgium). Maximum output was increased to 400PS/7,200rpm.

The ninth-generation Bluebird (U13) was launched on September 24, 1991. This distinctive model was available in 2 different body types (sedan & hardtop) and 3 clearly defined series - the SSS and EEX sedans, and the ARX hardtop. A characteristic of the styling of the sedan, with its fully-pressed door panels, was the uninterrupted mono-form design. Also, its body was larger: compared to the previous generation U12, the wheelbase was extended by 70mm and overall height was increased by 30mm. This, combined with the effect of the logical packaging , provided a spacious interior. In addition to 5 petrol engines (2,000cc/1,800cc, all twin-cam), there was a 2,000cc diesel engine, and the rear suspension was equipped with a super active toe control. Additionally, advanced noise-suppression technologies were adopted; these included strengthening the body using the weld-bond process, as well as adopting double vibration proof suspension and the world's first active noise control system (for canceling out low-frequency engine noise using sound of the opposite phase), installed on the ARX-Z Series. The sedan was available in 2 series: the sporty SSS and the family-orientated EEX. The 2000SSS-G was the top-of-the-line 2WD model powered by the SR20DE (145PS) engine. It was also equipped with aluminum wheels, fog lights, and driver's seat SRS airbag as standard.

"Caravan" is a traditional brand as Nissan cab-over van since 1973. Although included in the lineup, ambulance models of the first generation E20 and the second generation E23 in1980 were manufactured on a built-to-order basis and specification sheet was not included in catalogs. But catalogs of ambulances with many options became available from the third generation E24 in 1986 to respond to the increase in first-aid measures taken on-board by emergency medical technicians based on Emergency Life-Saving Technician's Act. This is an ambulance of "Hyper-Pack specification" with VG30E gasoline engine (V6, 3000cc), ambulance cot (stretcher), and Aero Sonic type warning light.

March (Micra in overseas) is a Nissan's leading compact car and the second generation March K11 was released in 1992. Its gentle styling of high quality got favorable reviews. The expected model life was unusual 10 years, which meant it had to have appealing characteristics. The lineup was; bodies of 3-door and 5-door and engines of 1000cc and 1300cc. Nissan's first continuously variable transmission system N·CVT was one of options for 1300cc model. The production of Micra K11 was started in UK in 1993. It became the first Japanese car of European Car Of The Year and became a big hit. This car is "i·z-f", the highest grade of 1-liter lineup with optional genuine aluminum wheels.

As turbo engines were banned from Group C cars in 1993, Nissan developed a naturally aspirated 3.5-liter engine, mounting it in the NP35 (JSPC specifications) and P35 (US IMSA specifications). However, this project was suspended when the World Championship was cancelled. As a result, the NP35 made just one appearance in the JSPC, while this P35 was doomed to become a phantom racecar.

The P35 was developed for the 1993 season, when turbo engines were banned. Like the NP35 (JSPC specifications), it was powered by a V12 3.5-liter NA (naturally aspirated) engine. US-based NPTI, which was in charge of basic chassis development, intended to enter the P35 in the 1993 IMSA Championship, but this never came about as Nissan pulled out of racing.

AUTECH JAPAN, Inc. has been standing out in areas of specialty vehicles, lifecare vehicles, and work-use vehicles since it was established as "a company that develops and produces cars of novel concept in small amount through the integrated system" in 1986. This is "Skyline Autech Version" manufactured by Autech Japan in 1992. It was based on "4-door sedan GTS-4" HNR32 with electronically controlled torque split type 4WD system, and mounted was RB26DE engine (naturally aspirated, 2600cc, 220ps). Engineers sticked to 4-door sedan as grand touring car and it gained a lot of attention as a car for an adult who loved sports driving. It featured front grille with crossrails like GT-R.

model: Nissan Sunny 1500 Super Saloon SV 60th Anniversary
model_full: Nissan Sunny 1500 Super Saloon SV 60th Anniversary (1993: FB13)
description: The first-generation Sunny (Datsun Sunny 1000) was released in 1966 as a concept for a 1-liter class basic sedan that was more compact than the Bluebird. From then, the Sunny led the Japanese affordable passenger car market for several decades, and from the 1970s, as a global car deployed in over 100 countries and regions, it overtook the Bluebird to become Nissan's highest-selling passenger car. The seventh-generation model, the B13 Series, released in 1990, appealed with its neat style and high quality as a normally evolved version of its predecessor, the "Trad Sunny" B12 Series. While only 4-door versions were available in Japan, there was also a sporty 2-door sedan in the overseas market. Meanwhile, a coupe version, the NX coupe, with individual styling by Nissan Design America was released at the same time. The car here is the mainstay "1500 Super Saloon" with special features to celebrate the 60th anniversary of Nissan's founding (1993).

model_full: Nissan Vanette Serena FX Rio (1993: C23)
description: The first generation "Vanette Serena" C23 rolled out in 1991 was a minivan of a new type that got favorable reviews for the semi-cab-over type body and practicality. It is the direct ancestor of "Serena" that has been on the market for more than 30 years. C23, developed based on the concept of "Family vehicle of the new generation that offers fun and comfortableness to all the passengers", became a big hit due to the endearing form, the interior space that generated a feeling of closeness, and the joy of driving created by the 4-wheel independent suspension and the midship layout. It is still remembered as a car that triggered the minivan boom in Japan in the 90s.

The ninth-generation Skyline (R33) was launched in August 1993, though the GT-R launch was slightly delayed: following its display in the autumn of 1993 at the 30th Tokyo Motor Show, it was finally launched in January 1995. This particular vehicle is the prototype displayed at the Tokyo Motor Show; the front and road-wheel design differ from the production model.

model: Skyline GT-R Gr. A: STP TAISAN No. 2
model_full: Skyline GT-R Gr. A: STP TAISAN No. 2 (1993: BCNR33)
description: In 1993, as many as seven GT-R machines participated in Japan Touringcar Championship (JTC) from Unisia JECS team (M. Hasemi/H. Fukuyama), Calsonic team (K. Hoshino/M. Kageyama) and other 5 teams. Audience was fascinated with battles between GT-R machines. GT-R would win as a matter-of-course, but which GT-R? That was the hottest topic. It was a revival of the age of Skyline 2000 GT-R that won 52 wins in 3 years from 1969. This is the genuine machine STP Taisan GT-R that won the 2nd round in 1993 and finished second in the 4th round driven by K. Takahashi, one of the leaders of car races in Japan since 1960s, and K. Tsuchiya, "Drift King", with popularity and ability.

The eighth generation Skyline R32 was rolled out in 1989, which became a hottest topic as the revival of "GT-R" after 16 years of discontinuation. R32 was entirely renovated from form to suspension. Sizes were reduced for higher dynamic performance, which was taken favorably as "return to Skyline as it should be" by many fans. The lineup was 4-door sedan and 2-door coupe. The original lineup was GT-R with the engine of 6-cyl. 2600cc DOHC twin turbo and models with 6-cyl. 2000cc OHC/DOHC/DOHC with turbo and with 4-cyl. 1800cc OHC. "GTS25" with newly developed engine of 6-cyl. 2500cc DOHC was added in 1991. This is 4-door sedan GTS25 TypeX·G in 1993.

March (Micra in overseas) is a Nissan's leading compact car and the second generation March K11 was released in 1992. Its gentle styling of high quality got favorable reviews. The expected model life was unusual 10 years, which meant it had to have appealing characteristics. The lineup was; bodies of 3-door and 5-door and engines of 1000cc and 1300cc. Nissan's first continuously variable transmission system N·CVT was one of options. The production of Micra K11 was started in UK in 1993. It became the first Japanese car of European Car Of The Year and became a big hit. This car is "i-z" with optional N·CVT, Viscous LSD, ABS, etc.

"Rasheen" is a compact 4WD that was exhibited at the 30th Tokyo Motor Show in 1993 and released in 1994. The unusual name came from the Japanese word "rashimban" meaning "compass" and the sales copy of the early days was "Our Anywhere Door." It was not a full-fledged 4WD but was a convenient city runabout and a pioneer of today's casual crossover SUV (crossover utility vehicle). It has been popular ever since its first release because of its pike-car-like atmosphere. Mounted engine was GA15DE of 1500cc in the early days and was changed to SR18DE of 1800cc at face-lift in 1997. Rasheen Forza, the sporty model with SR20DE engine of 2000cc and 145ps, was added in 1998.

The sixth generation Silvia S14 was rolled out in 1993 as the successor of popular S13 on the concept of "stylish sport coupe that realizes good taste and fun of driving-at-will". Although S13 was a compact car, S14 fell into the category of standard-sized car due to enlarged sizes to achieve roadholding ability, interior comfort, and collision safety. But styling image of popular S13 and grades of K's, Q's, and J's were kept in mind. S14 was popular as "240SX" in overseas markets. On the other hand, the hatchback model 180SX RS13 was rolled out in 1989 and manufactured until 1998. This car is "K's Type S" in 1994 with the rear spoiler equipped as standard and the turbo engine of 220ps.

model_full: Skyline GT-R Nürburgring Time Attack (1994: BCNR33)
description: The eighth generation Skyline R32 fell into the category of small-size cars except "GT-R" for touring car races. But the ninth generation Skyline R33 rolled out in 1993 was categorized as ordinary passenger car since the body was enlarged to represent "Mainstream grand touring car for outstanding driving pleasure". The new Skyline GT-R was exhibited as reference at Tokyo Motor Show in 1993 and released in 1995. This is a factory test car with the chassis No.000055. It was equipped with aluminum roll-over bar for time trial at Nürburgring, Germany. Its record was 7'59"887 which was faster than that of R32 by 21 sec. The copy "Fascinated by minus 21 sec." is still talked about.

The first generation Cefiro A31 was born in 1988 to be a personal car driven by its owner to enjoy driving. The second generation Cefiro A32 was rolled out in 1994. Its platform was integrated with that of Maxima, a large-sized FWD sedan, and the layout was changed to transverse FWD layout with VQ engine series (V6). This new Cefiro pursued higher level of "high traveling performance" and "comfortableness" of the previous generation. Lineup was cozy Excimo series and S Touring series for fun of driving. Engine variations were VQ20DE of 2000cc, 2500cc, and 3000cc. This is "30 S Touring" on which VQ30DE is mounted that generates 220ps.

Nissan stopped competing in the Le Mans after 1990, but NISMO took its place. Their Skyline-based GT car - NISMO GT-R LM - was entered for Le Mans in 1995 and 1996. In 1995, this No.22 car (H. Fukuyama/S. Kasuya) was 10th overall and 5th in its class. It was modified to 2WD (FR) drive, a better choice for heavy vehicles. And unlike the No.23 car, it was powered by a Group N specification engine.

model_full: NISMO GT-R LM Road Car (1995: BCNR33)
description: The only machines that can enter the 24 Hours of Le Mans race in the GT class are so-called GT cars, based on vehicles approved for use on public roads. Based on the Skyline GT-R, this vehicle was created as an official road car so NISMO could take part in the 1996 Le Mans; it was actually registered in the UK (although never marketed).

The first generation Primera P10 was rolled out in 1990 as a sedan of the new generation that realized both running performance and comfortableness. Primera was equipped with "front multilink suspension" for FWD drivetrain to enable high controllability that was one of the achievements of "Project 901" to develop high technologies. Other features included large interior space and spacious luggage room.The fun of driving it brought and conscientious works got very favorable reviews. It became legendary as a car that changed the image of Nissan in European markets. This car is the last model of P10, equipped with "2.0Tm·S selection" and optional full air spoiler package.

The tenth generation Bluebird U14 rolled out in 1996 is the model that shared platform with Primera P11. Traditional hardtop cars were discontinued, and neat sedan became the only body type available. Variations were sporty SSS series and formal Le Grand series, and engine variations were gasoline engine of 1800cc and 2000cc and diesel engine of 2000cc. Direct injection engine and Hyper CVT with 6-speed manual mode were added later to achieve power-up of engine, cut-down of emission, and higher fuel-efficiency. Implementation of dual SRS airbags on front seats and ABS as standard was a characteristic trend of the time. This car is "SSS Limited" with 150ps engine.

Since the appearance of the first-generation model 30 (announced in March 1960, launched in April), the Cedric - noted for its impressive styling and advanced automotive technologies - has stood at the forefront of Japanese automobile manufacture, securing an assured position of strength in a broad range of applications, from personal to formal. The seventh-generation Y31 was launched on June 17, 1987. Its development concept was focused on luxury car styling, creating the optimal balance of performance specifications, and generating a feeling of high quality throughout. True to the Cedric tradition of always adopting the newest technologies, the designers of this model went to great lengths to incorporate the latest advances, including a newly developed V6 twin-cam high-flow ceramic turbo engine, an electronically controlled air suspension, and a high-quality 4-coat paint process. There was a choice of a 4-door hardtop and a 4-door sedan; the latter could also be specified as a taxi. The three grades were Super Custom, Classic, and Original. At first the Y31 was available with either the RB20P LPG engine or the RD28 diesel engine, but as part of a minor change in June 1991 the NA20P 4-cylinder in-line LPG engine was added. At the same time, the vehicle design was modified to put more emphasis on rear-seat passengers, changing the roofline to increase headroom, and eliminating the opera windows. Adopted as standard equipment were halogen headlights with combined fog lights, a high-mount brake light, side-door beams, and a dual seat lifter for the driver.
NA
NA

1990 was the last year Nissan cars ran at 24 Hours of Le Mans. But Nissan and NISMO (Nissan Motorsports International Co., Ltd.) launched "3-Year Project: Challenge to Le Mans" in 1995. The displacement of RB26DETT engine of Skyline GT-R (BCNR33), inline 6-cylinder DOHC twin turbo, was increased to 2,795cc. The engine output of the works machines exceeded 600ps. This machine No.23 finished 15th (Overall) and 5th (Class) with the drivers M. Hasemi, K. Hoshino and T. Suzuki in 1996 with support from "Club Le Mans," the Nissan Motorsports Fan Club in Japan with NISMO at the core.

The UNISIA JECS Camino competed in the 1996 All Japan Touring Car Championships with the Sunny. The driver was Masahiko Kageyama. Its Japan Touring Car Championship debut was in round 3 in 1996. That season, it achieved its first win in JTCC Round 8 in MINE. There was a wide range of cars in this event, including the Corona EXiV, the Civic Ferio, Opel, and BMW.

In 1994, the leading super touring car in Europe entered the All Japan Championship. In the first year, following on from the Primera, the Sunny took part from the 11th (TI) event and in the following year the Xanavi Sunny (#31, A. Iida) won the 10th (Mine) event for the first time. This commemorative car is the Xanavi Sunny (#32, S. Motoyama) which competed in the 1996 season.

The second-generation Terrano was launched in September 1995. In January of the following year, it participated in the TOTAL Granada-Dakar Rally 1996 (aka: Paris-Dakar). This car is a replica of the machine which entered in the same rally by the Nissan Private Japon team. It was produced as a display car for the autumn 1995 Tokyo Motor Show. In the rally, the Ishihara/Saito team came in 60th place (9th in the T1 class), and the Takeda/Sugimoto team came in 62nd place.
NA
NA
NA

In mid-1990s, various approaches were discussed within Nissan to determine a new Z-car after 300ZX Z32. This is one of the prototypes manufactured based on left-hand-drive Nissan 240SX S14 (Silvia in Japan). KA24DE engine (4-cyl. inline) was tuned to generate 200ps in front mid-ship layout, and the form was Z-like nifty fastback style that created a unique charm. It is said that Mr. Y. Katayama (Mr. K), the father of Z-car, drove the car at Tochigi Proving Ground, felt a sense of unity with the car and DNA of Z, and liked it. Although being a stillborn model, it was stored in Nissan for more than 20 years and was restored by Nissan's prototype production section.

model_full: Nissan Patrol (Safari) 4-door Turbo Diesel Granroad (1997: WRGY61)
description: "Nissan Patrol" born in 1951 was the Nissan's first 4WD car and has been favored all over the world due to its rigidity and high traveling performance. 6 generations of Patrol models were rolled out in 70 years from 1951 to 2021. It was known as "Safari" from 1980 to the 2000s in Japan. Y61 rolled out in 1997 is known as the third generation "Safari" in Japan and as the fifth generation "Patrol" in overseas markets. Y61 featured the form with strength and modern senses, the comfortable ride, the traveling performance by the part-time 4WD system, and the power train that realized output and improved environmental performances. This car is Y61 with TD42 Turbo Diesel engine.

Having raced the Skyline GT-R in 1995 and 1996, Nissan (NISMO) decided to enter a newly developed GT car in 1997. In that year, following a closely fought contest with Porsche and McLaren, the No.23 car (K. Hoshino, E. Comas, Masahiko Kageyama) came in 12th overall, 5th in class. The R390 name was derived from the previous R380 GP machine.

Following on from NISMO, which raced the Skyline at Le Mans, Nissan developed a true racing car, the R390, and entered it in1997. That year it raced three cars; two retired, but car No.23 (K. Hoshino, E. Comas, Masahiko Kageyama) came in 12th. The No.21 car team included M. Brundle, J. Muller, and W. Taylor.

The new model Stagea rolled out in 1996 is a station wagon developed on the concept of "prestige touring wagon" to realize comfortable and sporty driving. The features were high traveling performance and large, user-friendly luggage room. "Autech Version 260RS" is a car rolled out by Autech Japan in 1997. 260 indicates that RB26DETT engine is mounted. This car fell into the grade of the highest performance with body and chassis vastly strengthened to accord with the power of 280ps. 260RS can be the fastest station wagon among Nissan cars since its constitution such as electric SUPER HICAS and electronically controlled torque split type 4WD is almost as good as that of the Skyline GT-R.

From 1994, the All Japan Touring Car Championship was contested in the Super Touring Car category (2,000cc, 4-door sedan). With the introduction of this new category, on a like-for-like basis made for a close contest and race became even more exciting. The Primera (P10), Sunny (B14), and Primera Camino (P11) all performed well.

GT-R V-spec was a Skyline GT-R with an optional package that was first equipped on Model R32 GT-R in February 1993. Its standard equipment included Brembobrakes and 17-inch BBS wheels. ATTESA E-TS PRO was adopted as the drive system for the all-new R33 GT-R rolled out in January 1995. GT-R V-specs cars were used a lot as a base car for Group N endurance races. This car is 1997 Skyline GT-R V-spec after the minor change in early 1997. Mounted is an inline 2.6-liter 6-cylinder DOHC twin turbo engine (RB26DETT) that is same as that of standard GT-R, but the car’s performances are more splendid due to the high performing brakes and larger wheels.
NA

Since the launch of the first-generation S30 (1969), the Fairlady Z became an exceptional hit as a sports car with a production total in excess of 1 million units. Special features of the fourth-generation model (Z32), launched in July 1989, included its spirited silhouette - wide proportions, slanted nose, and forward cabin. Both two-seater and 2/2 series were produced.

NISMO's "Le Mans challenge" continued for two years, 1995-96, but it is difficult to win at Le Mans with a production car like the Skyline. So from 1997 to 1999 Nissan took up the challenge using a purpose-built GT car. In 1998, the R390 GT1's second year at Le Mans, car No.32 (Hoshino, A. Suzuki, Kageyama) came in 3rd overall - Nissan's best result in this event.

In 1998, in its second attempt at Le Mans, the R390 GT1 was represented by a total of 4 entries: No.30 (Clarion), No. 31 (UNISIA JECS), No. 32 (Calsonic), and No.33 (JOMO). Its proved to be a difficult race, with only 23 cars completing the course, but all the Nissans made the top-ten ranking, with car No.32 (Hoshino, A. Suzuki, Kageyama) coming in 3rd overall, thus demonstrating the machine’s reliability.

model: Nissan R390GT1 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1998
model_full: Nissan R390GT1 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1998 (1998: R390)
description: Nissan R390GT1 is the racing car that was manufactured under GT1 regulations of the time to win 24 Hours of Le Mans in late 1990s. It finished 12th in the overall category at its first challenge in 1997, but in 1998 all the 4 participating machines finished in the top 10 in the overall category (No.32 steered by Kazuyoshi Hoshino, Aguri Suzuki and Masahiko Kageyama won 3rd, No.30 finished 5th, No.31 finished 6th, and No.33 finished 10th). This car is the genuine machine of No.32 of Nissan R390GT1 that won 3rd, the best record of Nissan at 24 Hours of Le Mans, in 1998. It was restored in 2018 to its original exterior.

Of the machines entered in the GT class of the 24 Hours of Le Mans race, at least one must be based on a vehicle that can be driven on public roads. Therefore this road car was created in order to obtain official type-approval for the R390 GT1 as a "GT car". It was never marketed, but it was rumored to be worth 100 million yen if it had been put on sale.

The tenth generation Skyline R34 made a debut in May 1998. The copy of the teaser campaign was so sensational; "BMW, Mercedes, or new Skyline?". Its biggest appealing point was, as the copy "Body is power. DRIVING BODY" said, improved body rigidity as a fundamental factor for joy of driving a car at will. Variations of R34 with traditional Skyline atmosphere and evolved performance were 2 types of body: 4-door sedan and 2-door coupe, 3 types of RB 6-cyl. inline engine: 2000cc, 2500cc naturally aspirated, and 2500cc turbocharged. "25GT FOUR" with torque split type 4WD "ATTESA E-TS" was also available. This car is 25GT Turbo of 4-door sedan in the early days.

model: Prairie Joy EV National Institute of Polar Research
model_full: Prairie Joy EV National Institute of Polar Research (1998: PM11rev.)
description: Nissan has a long history of the development of EV from Tama electric vehicle by “Tokyo Electro Automobile Co.” in 1947. In 1990s, Nissan decided to adopt the world's first commercialized lithium ion batteries by Sony Corporation and started joint development with Sony in 1992. The lease of this “Prairie Joy EV,” the world's first EV on the market with lithium ion battery, to companies started in 1997. It showed sufficient performance with the max. speed of 120km/h and mileage per charge of over 200km. Its large interior space of minivans was also favorable. This car was used to collect Arctic air at National Institute of Polar Research in Norway from 2000 to 2006 with no trouble.

Launched in September 1995, the second-generation P11, like its predecessor, used its advantage of an SR engine and multilink suspension to do well in the JTCC or Japan Touring Car Championship and in various European championship races. It also came 2nd in series at South East Asia Touring Car Zone Challenge in 1998, in which many different Asian countries competed.

Nissan has continued R&D of EV that originated from "Tama electric vehicle" in 1947 by Tokyo Electro Automobile Co. Nissan started to sell Cedric EV in 1991 and Avenir EV in 1994 mainly to companies. "Prairie Joy EV" was released in 1997 as the world's first car with lithium ion battery. This is "R'nessa EV" manufactured based on a minivan R'nessa (N30) and released in 1998. It was equipped with many technique elements such as flat floor, non-contact charging system, air conditioner with remote controller, EV-dedicated digital meters, lithium ion battery and permanent-magnet synchronous motor, all of which would be implemented in the first generation Leaf (ZE0) in later years.
NA

After appearing at the 1987 Tokyo Motor Show, the Zaurus took part in one-make races in 1989. This car is the successor model debuted in 1993. Designed as a true single-seater, it was used at the Nissan Racing School for advanced classes. The engine is the SR18DE, familiar from the Primera, which has a maximum output of 150PS at 6,400rpm.

From 1995, the All Japan GT Championship (JGTC) was split into two engine classes; the class names GT-500 and GT-300 were used from 1996 onwards. Cars such as the Skyline GT-R, Supra and NSX were classed as GT-500, while the Silvia, MR2 and the BMW were in the GT-300 category. This Silvia is a replica of the 1998 JGTC specification car sponsored by XANAVI Informatics Corp..

At the 1998 All Japan GT Championships, the E. Comas/Masami Kageyama team competed in a NISMO works machine (entry name: Pennzoil NISMO GT-R). Engine displacement was increased from 2,658cc to 2,708cc, and maximum output topped 500PS. In the 1998 season, Comas gained fame by taking the Driver's trophy.

model_full: Skyline GT-R Autech Version 40th Anniversary (1998: BCNR33)
description: This is the model released from Autech Japan, Inc. in commemoration of 40th anniversary of Skyline. It was exhibited at the 32nd Tokyo Motor Show in 1997 with the concept of "Sports sedan of highest performance for grown-ups" and released in 1998. It shared the body with 4-door Skyline R33 but rear doors and rear fender were newly designed only for this model to replicate blister fender of 2-door GT-R. The exterior with smaller front spoiler and no rear spoiler created placid atmosphere. The interior for 4 passengers with bucket type rear seats was also unique. It was the first 4-door Skyline GT-R since "2000GT-R (PGC10)" released in 1969, and got favorable reviews.

Nissan entered a pair of R391 machines in the 1999 24 Hours of Le Mans race, but car No. 22 crashed in the previous day's qualifier, and car No. 23 retired after seven hours. However, in November that year, car No. 23 (M. Krumm, E. Comas, S. Motoyama) vindicated the R391, wining a brilliant victory in the Le Mans-Fuji 1000km race held in Japan.

A boom in touring car races for 2-liter 4-door sedan cars happened around 1992 in European countries. In UK, BTCC (British Touring Car Championship) became very popular and the first generation PrimeraP10 that was manufactured in UK at the time also ran at races. The second generation P11 also raced at circuits. In 1999, machines such as Volvo S40, Renault Laguna, Vauxhall Vectra, Ford Mondeo and Honda Accord competed bitterly for their prestige. This machine is the genuine champion car that won 13 out of 26 races of BTCC in 1999 and got 4 titles such as Manufacturers', Drivers' and Teams'. The mounted engine is SR20DE with improved output of 300ps.

This vehicle, entered in the 1999 Japan GT Championship series, is the "Pennzoil NISMO GT-R", the NISMO works machine driven by the E. Comas/S. Motoyama team. Very stable at speed, it scored points in all 6 rounds of the series, and E. Comas took the Driver's trophy two years in a row. The drive system was modified to 2WD (FR).

Following "Prairie EV" (1996), Hypermini was rolled out at Tokyo Motor Show in 1997 and production model was released in 2000. It was a very compact EV for 2 passengers; the overall length of 2660mm and the minimum turning radius of 3.9m. It was equipped with the groundbreaking keyless entry system of IC card type with a view to car-sharing, and was actually used to collect data from car-sharing experiments in Yokohama and Ebina. The max. speed was 100km/h and the mileage per charge was 115km, sufficient for driving in the neighborhood. Run-flat tires and lightweight aluminum frame were also adopted. "Drive. Only 100 yen for 100 km" was the forward-looking sales copy.

The first generation Cube Z10, based on the second generation March/Micra K11, was a revolutionary model that realized spacious cabin for 4 people and high usability by tall, square wagon-type body and glass hatch. It was rolled out in 1998 and became a big hit since there were no similar compact cars in Japan at the time. Cumulative sales of the first generation Cube reached as many as 400,000 during 5 years from 1998 to 2002 when the second generation Z11 made a debut. It was a victory of concept that younger people in the late 1990s enjoyed their leisure time with friends and the new model should capture them. This is the highest grade 4WD Cube "X" with aluminum wheels as standard.

In the 2000 Japan GT Championship, GT-500 class, U. Katayama and M. Krumm competed in the series with this NISMO works machine (entry name: Castrol NISMO GT-R). That year, with the Comas/Kageyama team (Locktite NISMO GT-R) also performing well, NISMO achieved 2nd place in the Team category.

Skyline GT-R (BNR34) made a debut in January 1999. That is the last generation of "Skyline GT-R" as of 2019. "V?SpecII Nür" and "M?Spec Nür" named after Nürburgring where GT-R cars were developed were manufactured in 2002. They were the limited models and the number of production was 1,000 each. The former was aimed at sprint races while the latter, with significantly flexible suspensions, at endurance races. Mounted for both models was the engine based on N1 specs with equalized weight balance of pistons and connecting rods, and its cylinder head cover was colored gold. This car is "M?Spec Nür" of the special pale gold color.

The 10th generation Skyline R34 was rolled out in 1998. The body had high rigidity to improve motion performance while securing enough interior space in a smaller body. Its highest-level performance model "GT-R" was released in 1999. "V⋅spec" was the center of talks due to higher traveling performance achieved by exclusive aero parts, specifically tuned suspensions and active LSD, and styling like a racing car. V⋅spec II added in 2000 adopted carbon engine hood with *NACA duct and aluminum pedals which created spartan atmosphere. This car is V⋅spec II of the special color "Bayside Blue." *NACA duct: the shape of intake port developed by NACA, the predecessor of NASA

Since the 2nd Rally Raid Mongol tournament in 1996, Masahiro Hasemi made consecutive appearances with the R50 Terrano, winning the 1997 and 1999-2000 events. At the 2000 rally (August 14-21), which was a 3,583.10km race starting at Ulan Bator, Hasemi won with a 4-hour lead over a Russian Jeep in 2nd place.

A new type of minivan "Elgrand" E50 rolled out in 1997 was a pioneer of "full-sized minivan" that is extremely popular in Japan now. Developed based on the concept of "High-end minivan of the new generation", Elgrand had the massive form and the comfortable and spacious interior space. The flat floor realized by packaging FR layout and semi-cab-over type body enabled a passenger to walk between seats. Comfortable seats with a sense of high quality and luxury created a space for relaxation. E50 was a driving force behind the age of luxurious minivans in Japan and the accumulated sales volume exceeded 200 thousand until 2002 when the next generation E51 was rolled out.

The coupe convertible "Varietta" was added to the seventh generation Silvia S15 line in 2000. It was a groundbreaking car since, with electric-powered metal roof, it was an open-top car with beautiful long deck form when roof was completely stored and was a beautiful, traditional coupe when roof was closed. Noise barrier performance, heat shielding performance and anti-theft system were drastically improved from convertibles of the past. The body was designed and manufactured by Autech Japan as 2+2 car that was spacious enough for 4 occupants. Naturally aspirated SR20DE engine and 5-speed MT/4-speed AT enabled nimble running, which was one of selling points. This is Varietta colored in brilliant blue.

model_full: Nissan Fairlady Z Version ST (2002: Z33)
description: Z-car history once halted when the production of Z32 ended in August 2000. However, the existence of the world-famous Z-car was too big for Nissan to throw away - as it represented its corporate DNA. Soon after the discontinuation, the expectation for Z-car's revival was growing among the fans, car enthusiasts, even among Nissan employees as well. The all-new Z-car concept was unveiled at 2001 North American International Auto Show, in the middle of expectation. It acquired a high reputation due to its modernity and traditional "Z-ness" within the exterior and interior as well. The new Z-car, model Z33, went on sale in July 2002 in the U.S. and Japan. The Z33 continued until Dec. 2008, and sold over 250,000 units in total. This was far more volume than the Z32. This silver car is an early model of Z33.

March (Micra in overseas) has been a Nissan's leading compact car since 1982. The third generation March K12 rolled out in 2002 became popular due to traditional usability, unique and cute form, and 12 body colors named after food. It was the first car that adopted "Alliance B Platform" developed jointly with Renault after the alliance in 1999. It achieved excellent overall performance by adopting newly developed light and compact CR engine with high output, low fuel consumption, low emission and improved calmness along with B Platform. It was Nissan's first product to adopt a telematics service "CARWINGS" (today's Nissan Connect) and "Intelligent Key". This is the car colored in orange named "Paprika Orange".

The GT-R version of the tenth-generation Skyline (R34) was launched in January 1999. As with the R32 and R33, it performed well on the circuit, and in the 2002 Japan GT Championships it provided much excitement for its fans. This vehicle is the replica used by NISMO in the pre-season press conference; the coloring is the same as that applied to the #23 Castrol Pitwork GT-R (Masami Kageyama/E. Comas).

model_full: MOTUL PITWORK GT-R 2003 JGTC No. 22 (2003: BNR34)
description: In 2003, Skyline GT-R (BNR34) with V6 engine participated in Japan GT Championship (JGTC) as NISMO team. Although 6-cyl.in line engine was a symbol of Skyline GT-R, the engine length and the weight were limiting factors for performance improvement. Compact V6 engine brought revolutionary improvement of weight balance and lowering of center of gravity. 2003 was the last year for Skyline GT-R to run the race of GT500 class of JGTC because Fairlady Z (Z33) was to run in 2004. This is No.22 Motul Pitwork GT-R that, driven by Masami Kageyama and Richard Lyons, won Round 2 of JGTC held at Fuji International Speedway in 2003, and placed third in the drivers ranking.

The fifth generation Fairlady Z Z33 (350Z in overseas) was rolled out in 2002, 2 years after the discontinuation of Z32 in 2000. "Roadster" was added in 2003 like "Convertible" was added to Z32. The roof was not metal top that was becoming gradually popular at the time but traditional soft-top, and electrically opened/closed in about 20 seconds. Mounted engine was naturally aspirated VQ35DE (V6, 4-valve DOHC, 3498cc) like coupe models. This is a show car exhibited at overseas motor shows that slightly differs from the production model.

The eleventh generation Skyline V35 rolled out in 2001 was a GT car of the new generation with "FM package", i.e., small and light V6 engine was mounted in front midship layout. It was highly praised even in overseas markets as "INFINITI G35" for upgraded roadholding ability and ride achieved by weight distribution of 52:48. The first models were sedans with 2500cc/3000cc VQ direct injection engines. "Sedan 350GT-8" with 3500cc engine and 8-speed paddle shift was added in January 2002 and the long-waited 2-door coupe series with 3500cc engine was added in January 2003. They became very popular due to the flowing and stylish form and high traveling performance. This car is Coupe 350GT rolled out in 2003.

New SUV "X-TRAIL" rolled out in 2000 was planned and developed based on the concept of "joyous, comfortable, and handy 4WD for 4 people at the price of 2 million yen", targeting people of 20s and 30s who enjoyed outdoor sports. Although the vehicle sizes were moderate, well-constructed packaging realized interior space and luggage room larger than a bigger 4WD enough to carry 4 people and their luggage. Well-thought specifications such as "waterproof interior" got very favorable reviews. At a minor change in 2003, it adopted "Pop-up steering wheel" so that a driver could change clothes easily in the driver's seat. This is "X" with 2000cc engine colored in "burning red".

Cube, a pioneer of "compact high-body wagon", was rolled out in 1998. The second generation Z11, produced based on the concept of "magical box", shared "Alliance B Platform" with March K12 and was rolled out in 2002. The form was genial and "cubic with rounded corners". It featured asymmetric rear window and convenient back door that opened/closed like a refrigerator door. Due to those features and interior with increased comfortableness, it gained enduring popularity and became a big hit with the accumulated sales of 550,000 which exceeded that of the first generation. This is "SX 70th-II", the special car rolled out on Nissan's 70th anniversary in 2003.

Murano is a crossover SUV that was rolled out in US in 2002 and became very popular. It was rolled out in Japan in 2004 to meet the demand from the market. In that year, Nissan held a daring press conference, posting "SHIFT_", to unveil 6 new models including Murano at the same time, which became a hot topic and impressed Nissan's aggressive strategy. The form designed on the theme of "lively sculpture" was as flowing as coupe. The copy was "That sports car is SUV" to deliver a message that Murano was different from traditional rugged SUV and was a new category itself. This is 350XV with the engine of 6-cyl. V-type 3500cc and genuine leather seats in bright copper color.

model_full: Nissan Pickup Dakar Rally 2004 mockup (2004: D22rev.)
description: The first Dakar Rally was held in 1978. Machines started the race in Paris, went through Algeria, Niger, and Mali, and reached Dakar in Senegal. The total driving distance was about 10,000km. In spite of cancellation and venue changes in between due to political reasons, the extremely grueling competition named "Dakar Rally" still continues.* The first NISSAN machine that participated in the rally was "Patrol" 160 in 1982. Then, Terrano/Pathfinder WD21 repeatedly won in T1 class and the second generation R50 won class championship in 2001. Pickup D22 by Nissan Works participated in the race from 2003 to 2005 and the best result was the 4th place. This is a mockup of 2004 model for display. * As of 2025

Luxury middle-sized sedans "Laurel" and "Cefiro" were integrated to be "Teana" in 2003. Based on the concept of "Luxury sedan for refined adults", it realized "the classy interior like a modern living room", featuring wood panels that created calmness and newness, and luxurious-sofa-like seats. As for exterior, it had a well-proportioned and graceful form to match up with interior. The copy "Modern living room in a car" that plainly conveyed the idea of design became a hot topic and the car received Good Design Award in 2003. The first generation Teana got favorable reviews also in the Asian market and became a hit with the global production of 300 thousand until 2008.

model_full: Xanavi NISMO Z 2004 JGTC No. 1(2004: Z33)
description: Skyline GT-R that won its last JGTC race in 2003 was replaced with Fairlady Z (Z33) as GT500 machine for JGTC races in 2004. Its main mechanisms such as VQ engine and transaxle were passed down from GT-R, and the styling was based on the limited model "Type E" with extended front/rear bumpers. The latter engine was peaky and could be made to do great things–sixth overall at the 24 Hours of LeMans in 1970, for example–but its low take rate demanded a more suitable replacement. This came in 1973, when the fuel-injected variant of Volkswagen’s air-cooled Type 4 engine was dropped in behind the two seats, staying there through 1976, when series production ended. When the 993’s M64/05 engine went into production it was rated at 272 horsepower at 6,100 rpm and 243 pound-feet of torque at 5,000 rpm. The Porsche LMP1-H (Le Mans Prototype Class 1, Hybrid) race car featured a hybrid system that consisted of a turbocharged 2.0V4 petrol engine at the rear axle and an electric motor at the front axle. The electric motor/generator unit (MGU) collected the energy from the front axle under braking and the AER exhaust energy recovery system operated on the exhaust gas – a separate turbocharger ran an alternator. The 2-litre engine sounds like a very small one, but the air flow into the engine was not restricted and up to 4 bar/58 PSI turbo boost pressure was allowed. By the new rules, the instant fuel consumption was limited and therefore the 2-litre engine was the effective choice. The Energy Recovery System (ERS) stored the energy in a battery until the driver activated the electric motor on the front axle.

description: Porsche Exclusive Manufaktur has worked with Brazilian aircraft builder Embraer for a limited-run of private jet-inspired 911 Turbo S cars, according to EVO. The special division is known for its astonishing creations, and this one is perhaps it’s most impressive. The collaboration will yield just 10 cars worldwide. They will be available for purchase by all buyers of the Embraer Phenom 300E business jet, which runs just under £8m. There has been no pricing information discussed for the car, but as you can imagine, the price for the target buyers likely isn’t a concern. The paint scheme for these cars matches the jet. The car combines gloss and satin-gloss finishes for the first time ever on an official 911 build. There are also blue pinstripes designed to match the aircraft. The wheels on these 911 Turbo S models are dark silver with the same blue accents. There’s a unique logo that references the aircraft. It’s on the exterior and the interior of the car. The car also gets each jet’s registration number on the underside of the 911’s active rear wing, which is painted in Speed blue. The engine for this car is the same as the regular 911 Turbo S, which is a 3.8-liter twin-turbocharged flat-six that puts out 641 hp and 590 lb-ft of torque. It has the ability to rocket the car from 0 to 62 mph in 2.7 seconds and all the way to a 205 mph top speed. Inside there’s plenty of blue that features in small quantities on the exterior of the car. There’s also plenty of black and chalk leather upholstery used throughout the car. It’s designed to match the cockpit of the jet. The key for the car is also painted in Speed blue and will feature the registration number of the corresponding jet. The car also comes with a special cover and a’1919 UC Globetimer Embraer’ watch.
